texts: Indonesian President Joko Widodo has confirmed that the executions of drug smugglers Andrew Chan and Myuran Sukumaran are imminent, as all legal appeals have been exhausted. The pair, along with eight other death row prisoners, are awaiting the conclusion of their appeals before they face the firing squad. President Widodo has stated that the executions will take place as soon as all legal procedures have been completed. Chan and Sukumaran are currently in an isolated cell on Nusakambangan Island, where they have lodged a challenge with the Constitutional Court to have their death sentence overturned. The executions have been delayed due to the Asian African conference being held in Jakarta this week.

A heartfelt letter written by a passenger to a pilot thanking them for safely bringing her home has gone viral on Twitter, just a week after the Germanwings tragedy. The letter, written by a passenger known as 'Bethanie', expresses her gratitude to the pilot and airline for allowing her to live in Spain while splitting her time with family in England. The letter has been shared over 3,700 times and has been favourited almost 3,000 times, with many praising the role of the pilot. The letter was written in light of the recent Germanwings plane crash, where pilot Andreas Lubitz deliberately crashed the plane, killing all 150 people on board, including three Britons. Investigations are continuing into the events of that fateful day. The letter has been shared by pilot Jai Dillon, who was shown the letter by a colleague in the industry. He praised the positive message and shared it on Twitter. The letter has been praised for its compassionate and understanding message.

Japan's Defense Minister Gen Nakatani has assured MPs that the country has never been invaded by aliens and that no government studies into extra-terrestrials are underway. The assurance came after an enquiry from an MP, Antonio Inoki, who had asked if aircraft were dispatched to meet extra-terrestrial visitors and whether studies on aliens were ongoing. Inoki had once seen a mysterious flying object in the sky. Nakatani said that the Air Self Defense Force scrambles fighter jets when there are indications of unidentified flying objects in Japanese airspace, but no alien visitors have been found. In 2007, the Japanese government had issued a statement saying they had not confirmed the existence of unidentified flying objects believed to have come from anywhere other than Earth, but the statement was later rebutted by the top government spokesman who believed that UFOs controlled by alien life-forms exist.

A growing recruitment crisis in secondary schools is causing vacancies in core subjects such as English, maths and science, with some posts attracting only one or two applicants. Headteachers warn the situation is likely to worsen due to the rise in pupil numbers and greater competition for graduates among employers. London schools are experiencing the most problems finding teachers in English, maths and science, followed by the North West and East of England. The non-core subjects facing recruitment difficulties include geography, design and technology, business studies, computer science, religious education and modern foreign languages. The survey received 97 responses from headteachers and groups of headteachers from local networks of schools. Schools are struggling to recruit credible candidates for maths, physics and English, and the union is proposing an expansion in school-led teacher training, the development of a core curriculum for teaching degrees and the launch of a campaign to attract new recruits. The next government must act urgently to ensure effective processes are put in place to model numbers of teachers needed in each sector and region, and promote the status and value of teaching as a profession.

An Indian salesman is facing up to seven years in prison and a fine of up to one million dirham for allegedly cursing Islam and the Prophet Mohammad on Facebook. The man, identified only as S.G., is accused of posting a 'blasphemous' status after watching a news bulletin about the war in Iraq. If found guilty, he could face imprisonment, a fine, or both. The man claimed he received the offending image over Whatsapp, but later admitted to posting the status on Facebook. The case was adjourned until April 27. Blasphemy is considered deeply offensive in the United Arab Emirates, and authorities routinely censor materials that contain blasphemous statements or anything critical of Islam. In 2011, a British tourist was taken to court for calling the Islamic prophet Mohammad a 'terrorist' during an argument in a shopping center.

A father from Coventry, Marcin Wasniewski, miraculously escaped death when his car crashed into the back of a lorry on the A444. Emergency services were shocked to find him walking away from the scene with only cuts and bruises. The car had embedded itself into the back of the lorry and paramedics were amazed that he had escaped serious injuries. Marcin believes that Jesus Christ saved him that day and is currently volunteering at a Christian centre while he recovers from his injuries. The crash would have been fatal if the impact had been just a couple of inches closer to the driver. Marcin suffered a deep scar on his face and an injured left arm. He is currently unable to work but is volunteering at the Christ Celebration Centre in Foleshill. He also spoke of how he remembers the night of the accident but not the crash itself. Paramedics were stunned by the outcome of the crash and described how the trailer had embedded itself into the windscreen of the car. They added that if the impact had been a couple of inches further across into the driver's side or if there had been a passenger in the car, the outcome would have been fatal.

An enormous European eagle owl has been terrorizing the Dutch town of Noordeinde for months, launching itself from rooftops onto unsuspecting birdwatchers' heads. The bird, which is believed to have escaped from an aviary, has been associated with humans and food, leading to a spate of attacks. Locals have been advised to arm themselves with umbrellas and twitchers have flocked to the town to catch a sighting of the impressive bird. The European eagle owl is one of the largest species of owls and has a maximum total wingspan of 75 cm. The wild owl, which weighs around 6lbs, spends an average of one minute perched on the head of innocent bystanders before flying off in search of the next perch. Photographers have been visiting the town to capture the owl's unusual behavior. The rogue owl has been causing chaos in the town for months and is believed to be behind a spate of vicious attacks. The European eagle owl is found in a variety of habitats but mostly lives in mountain regions, coniferous forests, steppes and other relatively remote places. The owl's unusual behavior has made it a popular attraction for twitchers.

A 100-year-old man from New Jersey allegedly killed his 88-year-old wife with an ax while she slept before committing suicide with a knife. The couple had a history of domestic issues, but a motive for the apparent murder-suicide has not been determined. Neighbors were visibly upset after the discovery of the bodies on Monday morning. The couple had been experiencing some domestic issues in recent years, and the wife had wanted to move to Florida full-time, but her husband wanted to keep their New Jersey home. Police had been to the house a few times in recent years, and the husband was reportedly suffering from dementia. The daughter had asked her mother to move home due to her husband's mental instability. The couple's relative discovered the bodies and called the police. Michael Juskin is one of the oldest people ever to be accused of homicide. The investigation is ongoing.

Sherrell Dillion, a single mother from Benefits Street, has landed a place in the Top Model of Colour competition despite being currently homeless. She has been striving for a career in modelling for years and hopes this will be her big break. She wishes her former neighbour White Dee all the success in the world and hopes to use the show to better herself. She recently became homeless after her house became infested with mice and is now living in temporary accommodation in Handsworth while she finds a permanent home. The final of Top Model of Colour UK takes place on May 30 and the winner will receive a modelling contract, jewellery, clothes and shoes as well as other prizes. Previous winners have been signed by major mainstream modelling agencies and graced some of the top magazines in the world.

A border guard was killed in a cross-border fire exchange with militants in Yemen this week, marking Saudi Arabia's first publicly known military death since it launched airstrikes against rebels inside its southern neighbor. Houthi rebels seized the presidential palace in the southern Yemeni port city of Aden, and Yemeni special forces loyal to former President Ali Abdullah Saleh arrived in an attempt to secure the city. U.S. Navy warships were patrolling off Yemen in search of suspicious shipping in the region, and a Panamanian-registered cargo ship was found to be carrying cement and construction materials. Hospitals in Aden are struggling to keep up with the intense fighting and chaos, and a hospital near heavy fighting was forced to shut down. Additionally, Al Qaeda fighters were reported to have freed 270 prisoners from Yemeni prisons. The situation in Yemen is extremely fluid and complicated.

The losses are due to fines and compensation for mis-sold financial products, as well as a slump in the value of premises in the US. RBS warned that it faces another ‘tough year’ and that there are still many conduct and litigation issues to be dealt with. The losses are a blow to taxpayers, who own 80% of the bank, and come at an awkward time for Chancellor George Osborne, who had hoped to show that the banks bailed out by taxpayers under the Labour government in 2008 were returning to profit. Kenny Bayless, a veteran referee from Las Vegas, has been appointed to oversee the highly anticipated Mayweather vs. Pacquiao fight on May 2. Bayless has refereed several high-profile fights involving both fighters in the past and has a reputation for being fair and unflappable. The Nevada State Athletic Commission has put their trust in Bayless to ensure a fair and impartial decision, as the fight is expected to attract a large audience beyond the usual boxing fans. Bayless will be joined by three judges, including Glenn Feldman from Connecticut, Dave Moretti from Las Vegas, and Burt Clements from Reno. Bayless and the judges will each receive a higher than expected payment for their services. The fight is expected to be a 12-round bout and will be the first time the two eight-division champions will face each other in the ring.

A Chinese hospital is being moved eight meters a day on 1,000 metal rollers to avoid demolition for a new road. The two-storey brick hospital outpatient building in Zhengzhou, Henan Province, is 1,700 square meters in size and requires more than 1,000 wheels to move. Engineers aim to move the building 17.5 meters south to its new spot. The project is expected to be completed in a few days and is not the first time engineers in China have carried out such a move. In 2013, a six-storey building in Shanghai was moved 38 meters with the help of 18 lifting jacks, and in 2004, the Fu gang Building in Guangxi Province was moved 36 meters and took 11 days to complete. The building is placed on metal plates with cylinder-shaped rollers wedged between them.

Real Madrid's teen sensation Martin Odegaard was left starstruck when he met former Brazil international Ronaldo at the club's training ground. Odegaard, who joined Real Madrid in January, has been training with the first team regularly and was in awe of the former World Cup winning striker. Ronaldo, who spent five years at Real Madrid, was visiting his old club ahead of their Champions League quarter-final second-leg clash against Atletico Madrid. Odegaard has found life tough at the Spanish giants in recent weeks, with first team coach Zinedine Zidane dropping him from the Castilla side after a downturn in results. Real Madrid are desperate for the Castilla side to win promotion to the second tier of Spanish football and Zidane must decide whether Odegaard's presence in the side is hindering their chances. Odegaard joined Real Madrid for £2.3million and signed a long-term £40,000 a week contract. He has trained with the likes of Cristiano Ronaldo and Gareth Bale and is said to be on a different wave length to his Castilla team-mates.

An inquest is set to take place this week regarding the death of Margaret Hesketh, a 70-year-old woman who was allegedly told she had terminal cancer by doctors but later found to have died of pneumonia while malnourished. The family claims that doctors had removed her feeding tubes and put her on a discredited Liverpool Care Pathway-style treatment for the dying, despite no evidence of cancer in a post-mortem. Doctors had initially ruled out surgery due to her poor health and had told the family that she had less than three months to live. The hospital has since confirmed that they disregarded the Liverpool Care Pathway in July 2014. The family is calling for a criminal investigation and want answers as to why Mrs Hesketh died in this way. The hospital has stated that more information will emerge at the public inquest.

Barcelona secured a vital win over Celta Vigo in La Liga, with Neymar, Dani Alves and Adriano all playing their part. The trio were seen wearing matching denim outfits in a post-match Instagram photo, with Neymar declaring 'we got home...important victory...Congratulations guys!!! Vamo to top.' Dani Alves also posted a similar picture, with Mathieu admitting his side were poor but still managing to secure the three points. Mathieu praised Gerard Pique for his impressive defensive display and the team returned to the summit of La Liga. The three Brazilians all started and played a crucial role in the win.

Aydian Ethan Dowling, a transgender man from Oregon, is the frontrunner to become the first transgender cover star of Men's Health Magazine. He has a significant lead in the publication's annual Ultimate Guy Search, with over 40,000 votes. The competition aims to find a man who embodies the qualities of a well-rounded, active, health-conscious and thoughtful guy. Aydian, who transitioned in 2009, is a role model for the LGBTQ+ community and has launched his own sportswear brand, Point5cc. He is confident that he has what it takes to win over the magazine's judging panel and make history as the first transgender cover star. If he wins, he would follow Iraq war veteran and amputee Noah Galloway, who clinched the top spot last year. Aydian is an active outdoorsman and enjoys hiking with his wife of three years, Jenilee. He is determined to find peace within his soul and overcome any challenges that come his way. The public vote only counts for 10% of the vote, but Aydian is confident that he has the support of the readers and the judging panel. If he wins, he would make history as the magazine's first transgender cover star.

Manchester Airport temporarily suspended flights today after a drone was reported in the area, causing disruption for hundreds of travellers. All flights were halted for about 20 minutes while police searched the area for evidence of the drone. Flights resumed after the search failed to turn up any evidence. Unmanned drones have become a serious problem for airports and pilots due to their increasing popularity and potential danger. The Civil Aviation Authority has successfully prosecuted two drone operators for safety breaches. Drones cannot be flown beyond the normal unaided line of sight of the operator, must always be flown at least 164ft away from a person, vehicle, building or structure, and must never be flown within 492ft of a congested area or large group of people. Police continue to investigate the report of the sighting.

YouTube is celebrating its 10th anniversary this year, and has become a major platform for content creators. The site gets billions of views every day, and the most popular channels draw larger audiences than many TV networks. To improve the quality of its content, YouTube has invested in "YouTube Spaces," which provide professional studios, training, and resources to creators. These spaces are available for free to YouTube partners, who create content and share ad revenue with the website. Anyone can create a YouTube channel, and the most popular ones, like Swedish gamer PewDiePie, have millions of subscribers. Japanese film and TV company Toei is partnering with YouTube to encourage more Japanese samurai dramas, or Jidaigeki, in order to attract new subscribers in one of YouTube's biggest markets. The goal is to raise the bar for YouTube content and attract more viewers. If a video goes viral, the financial rewards can be significant, with thousands of creators earning six-figure incomes and a few earning in the millions.

Sutherland Council is exploring the possibility of allowing overseas backpackers to camp in allocated locations on popular beaches in order to boost the local economy and deter them from neglecting certain areas due to a lack of accommodation. The proposal has been met with mixed reactions from locals, with some welcoming the economic boost and others concerned about the potential for disorderly behavior and the impact on land values. The council is considering the idea of rezoning open park areas to accommodate the campers, but some believe this may not be feasible. The proposal aims to solve the issue of younger visitors parking their vans illegally on the streets and encourage seasoned travelers, retirees, and campervan users to the area. However, some local business owners are skeptical about the feasibility of the proposal.

Jordan Henderson has signed a new five-year £100,000-a-week contract with Liverpool, committing his long-term future to the club. He had previously been linked with a move away from Anfield in 2012, but has since proven himself and become a key player for the Reds. Henderson is determined to help Liverpool win trophies and is hopeful of being handed the captain's armband when Steven Gerrard leaves. Liverpool boss Brendan Rodgers is hoping other players, including Raheem Sterling, will follow Henderson's lead and sign new deals. Henderson arrived from Sunderland in 2011 and has become an important player for the Reds.

A 16-year-old boy from Mossley, Greater Manchester, has pleaded guilty to attempting to buy the biological toxin abrin from the dark web. The dark web is a subsection of the deep web, used for sharing information and trading goods anonymously and encrypted. The teenager was caught after expressing an interest in acquiring the toxin and was aware of its toxicity and potential for harm. He will be sentenced later this month for the offence, which is contrary to the Criminal Attempts Act 1981 and Section 1 of the Biological Weapons Act 1974. The dark web has been used for illegal activities such as selling drugs and hacked information. Last year, a graphic designer was the first person to be prosecuted under the Biological Weapons Act for attempting to poison her mother with a substance obtained from the dark web.

Georgia Governor Nathan Deal signed a bill on Thursday that will legalize low-THC cannabis oil for certain medical conditions, such as medication-resistant epilepsies. This bill, known as Haleigh's Hope Act, will create an infrastructure, registration process, and research program for the drug. The bill is named after Haleigh Cox, a 5-year-old girl who moved to Colorado to receive medical marijuana for her seizures after her condition worsened despite taking five potent drugs. The bill will benefit not only people with chronic seizure disorders but also allow patients to receive in-state treatment. The law is specific to a handful of conditions, but medical marijuana is legal in nearly half the states, and doctors are increasingly studying its effects on various ailments. However, under federal law, marijuana remains illegal to grow, sell, or use for any purpose. This presents a Catch-22, as marijuana is restricted due to a lack of research, but research is difficult to conduct due to tight restrictions.

Historian David Starkey has made controversial statements about ethnic minorities, disabled people, and women in an interview with the Daily Telegraph. He criticized Baroness Doreen Lawrence for treating minorities as victims and claimed women tend to be of average intelligence. He also expressed his views on the current political class and the state of liberation movements. Starkey, who is born with disabilities, believes that people should not be portrayed as victims and fears of Islamophobia are victimizing Muslims. His comments have sparked controversy and criticism.

Newcastle United fans are planning to boycott the club's next home game against Tottenham on April 19 in protest against owner Mike Ashley. A social media campaign has been launched, encouraging fans to turn up in the lowest ever Premier League crowd. A website, Sack Ashley.com, has been set up to promote the boycott and protests have also received the support of the Newcastle United Supporters Trust. Fans who don't want to boycott the game are encouraged to take part in demonstrations before and after the game. Newcastle boss John Carver suffered a fourth successive defeat at Sunderland on Sunday. The boycott and protests have been initiated due to fans' frustration with Ashley's ownership and their desire for increased supporter representation/ownership.

Demi Moore is selling her Manhattan penthouse apartment, which she once shared with ex-husband Bruce Willis, for a record-breaking $75million. The 14-bedroom apartment includes 7,000 square feet of living space and wrap around terraces with views of Central Park and the Hudson River. The couple purchased the apartment in 1990 and decorated it in a Southwestern mission motif. They split up in 2000 and Moore no longer spends much time there. The apartment and a two-bedroom maisonette are being listed by Adam D Modlin of the Modlin Group. The San Remo building was designed in 1929 and turned into a co-op in 1972. Neighbors include Dustin Hoffman, Diane Keaton, Steven Spielberg and U2 frontman Bono. The combined monthly maintenance fees for both residences is more than $20,000. If the penthouse sells for $75million, it will break the record for the most expensive co-op apartment ever sold on the Upper West Side. Moore and Willis were married from 1987 until 2000 and share three daughters.

McDonald's announced plans to raise wages for its employees at company-owned restaurants in the US, starting July 1. The average wage is expected to be more than $10 an hour by the end of 2016, up from the current rate of $9 an hour. McDonald's USA owns about 10 percent of the more than 14,300 McDonald's restaurants across the country, with the rest operated as franchises that will not be subject to the pay increases. The company said the increase is part of an effort to be the most competitive and attractive employer. In addition to wage increases, McDonald's says workers at company-owned stores will get paid time off. McDonald's US business has been struggling, with sales and customers counts at established locations falling two years in a row. The company named Steve Easterbrook as its new CEO in January. McDonald's also said it is expanding benefits to help workers at company- and franchise-owned restaurants complete high school and college. The move was criticized by some workers as not enough to make a real difference. McDonald's has been facing public pressure to increase wages and allegations of violations including denial of overtime pay and unsafe working conditions. The economy has continued to strengthen, with the unemployment rate falling from 6.7 percent to 5.5 percent over the last year. McDonald's USA President Mike Andres said the demonstrations did not affect the company's reputation. Labor organizers with a campaign to raise fast food industry wages to $15 an hour say they are fighting to unionize low-wage workers across various sectors.

More than 1,700 Chinese students took an exam in their high school's playground due to a lack of indoor space. The students suggested and organized the outdoor exam themselves, and many believed it was a novel way to broaden their horizons and encourage relaxation. The school saw it as a test of the students' organizing capacity. The students took turns to avoid being dazzled by the sun and some believed it could help prevent cheating. The unusual move was seen as a way to encourage the students to think outside the box.

A known child sex offender, Patrick James Fredricksen, 30, has been arrested in Utah on suspicion of stealing a school bus and attempting to abduct young children. Fredricksen, who has previous convictions for unlawful sexual activity with a minor and impersonating a firefighter, was stopped on his way to one child's home. He had already used the bus's on-board list of children's names and addresses to try and abduct a young girl. Fredricksen is also expected to face a charge of damaging a prison after breaking a sprinkler pipe inside his cell and flooding the booking area. His crime spree is alleged to have started while he was working for a landscaping firm at a baseball complex. He is on Utah's Sex Offender Registry after pleading guilty in 2004 to unlawful sexual activity with a minor. He was also charged in 2005 with sexual exploitation of a minor and dealing in material harmful to a minor but the case was dismissed as part of an apparent plea bargain. In 2006, he was living in Salt Lake County when he pleaded guilty to impersonating a fireman. He had previously worked as a volunteer firefighter for the Huntington Fire Department but was dismissed in 2003 for stealing clothing and equipment. After his dismissal, he pinned on a stolen badge and lent a hand at emergencies, the court was told. He also stole firefighting equipment and used his fake status to rent an apartment and get credit. He was sentenced to 36 months of probation and ordered to have counselling. Fredricksen is currently in Emery County Jail for investigation of theft of a vehicle and attempted child kidnapping.

Former U.S. Marine Charlie Linville, who lost his right leg and several fingers in an explosion in Afghanistan, is attempting to climb Mount Everest for the second time to inspire others with disabilities. Liana Barrientos, a 39-year-old woman from New York, is facing criminal charges for allegedly participating in an immigration scam by getting married 10 times between 1999 and 2010. Prosecutors say that some of her husbands filed for permanent residence status shortly after the marriages, and that any divorces occurred only after the filings were approved. Barrientos is believed to still be married to four men, and at one time was married to eight men at once. She is facing two criminal counts of offering a false instrument for filing in the first degree, and if convicted, could face up to four years in prison. The case was referred to the Bronx District Attorney's Office by Immigration and Customs Enforcement and the Department of Homeland Security's Investigation Division. Seven of her husbands are from so-called "red-flagged" countries, and her eighth husband was deported in 2006 to his native Pakistan after an investigation by the Joint Terrorism Task Force. Barrientos pleaded not guilty in court on Friday and was arrested for allegedly sneaking into the New York subway through an emergency exit. Her next court appearance is scheduled for May 18.

Mauricio Pochettino believes Harry Kane should win the PFA Player of the Year award over Eden Hazard due to his impact on English football. Kane has had an impressive season for Tottenham and could become the first Spurs player to score 30 goals in a season since Gary Lineker. Pochettino defended the club's decision to play a one off pre-season game against the MLS All Stars in Colorado, stating it is only one game and a good test for the team. Kane has scored 29 goals in all competitions for Tottenham this season and will have to beat Hazard to claim the individual gong. Other nominees include Diego Costa, Alexis Sanchez, David de Gea, and Philippe Coutinho.

A 66-year-old man was arrested and charged with public nuisance and a breach of the peace after allegedly burning an Australian flag at the Shrine of Remembrance in Brisbane's Anzac Square on Friday afternoon. The incident occurred just days before the 100th Anzac Day commemoration services, where tens of thousands of people are expected to gather around the Eternal Flame of Remembrance to pay their respects to fallen service men and women. The man's actions have been condemned by veterans and the Returned and Services League (RSL). He will face Brisbane Magistrate's Court on Saturday morning. This incident follows weeks after protesters were seen burning the Australian flag at anti-Islamic and anti-racism protests in Melbourne. The man's arrest comes at a time when Anzac Day commemoration services are being held around the country. Big screens are being set up around Anzac Square, Post Office Square, King George Square and Queen Street Mall to ensure that everyone who attends the dawn service gets a glimpse of the moving service. Dawn services will start at 4.28am at the Shrine of Remembrance in Adelaide Street's Anzac Square.

Manchester City manager Manuel Pellegrini is urging his team to make a big-money signing this summer in order to keep up with their rivals. City were hampered last summer by UEFA's Financial Fair Play regulations, which included a £49million net spending cap. Pellegrini believes that Manchester City must sign a 'crack' player, such as striker Sergio Aguero, in order to stay competitive. Despite the team's current fourth place position in the Premier League, Pellegrini still believes they have a chance of retaining the title. He is also concerned with the team's league position and wants them to finish at the top of the table. Pellegrini has not yet indicated whether a spending spree will be sanctioned.

Richard Sherman and his girlfriend Ashley Moss welcomed a son, Rayden, just four days after the Seattle Seahawks lost the Super Bowl to the New England Patriots. Sherman shared photos of his newborn son on Instagram and also congratulated Patriots quarterback Tom Brady. Despite the loss, Sherman was named the NFC Defensive Player of the Year by the Kansas City Committee of 101. He is currently undergoing surgery to repair a torn ligament in his left elbow and will return to the field in August. The Seahawks will play the Denver Broncos in their first preseason game as they aim to make it to the Super Bowl for the third consecutive season.

A 29-year-old man named Pankaj Saw died after falling from an apartment balcony in Macquarie Park while on the phone with his new wife in India. It is believed that the wooden railing gave way, causing him to fall three storeys to his death. Saw was in Australia on a long-stay work visa and had been working on and off in Sydney in recent years. Friends and colleagues remember him as a man full of life and energy. Investigators are looking into whether a structural fault contributed to the fatal fall and are hoping to speak to the person who helped Saw before paramedics arrived. The director of Housesafe believes that the collapse was an accident waiting to happen due to the railing not being installed in a safe and compliant manner. The balcony and unit's structure are being investigated for any potential faults.

An autopsy has revealed that a teenager killed by police in Illinois on Saturday was shot twice in the back. Justus Howell, 17, was chased down the street by police responding to an argument before being shot. Witnesses reported hearing an officer say they had shot the boy, but it is not known if an officer has been suspended while the shooting is investigated. The teenager's mother, LaToya Howell, described her son as wanting to be a surgeon and said he was fleeing from police when he was killed. The Zion police chief did not return calls seeking comment on the autopsy results. Toxicology results are pending.

Robert Durst, a jailed millionaire and suspected murderer, pleaded not guilty to a new federal charge of gun possession on Tuesday. Durst is also facing a murder charge in California and two state weapons charges in Louisiana. He claims that his previous convictions in Pennsylvania do not make it illegal for him to carry a gun under Louisiana law. Durst is currently being held without bail in a state prison due to his suicide risk. The arrest in New Orleans is believed to have been timed to coincide with the conclusion of HBO's 'The Jinx' series. Durst was arrested last month on suspicion of the 2000 murder of his friend Susan Berman. The hearing had a bizarre moment when Durst asked the prosecutor who he was. Durst's lawyers are discussing another federal matter regarding two FBI agents and a state trooper on an FBI task force. Durst's lawyers claim that his arrest in New Orleans was illegal and that his room was searched without a warrant. Durst had been lying low and registered at the Marriott under the name Everette Ward. Authorities found a passport, a head-and-chest latex mask, a handgun, and marijuana in his room. Durst's lawyers are yet to file their response to the federal matter. Durst is currently facing multiple charges and is being held without bail.

Wigan secured their first away win of the season with a 40-22 victory over Wakefield, thanks to a hat-trick from Joe Burgess. Despite the win, Wigan's coach Shaun Wane was not pleased with his team's performance and was further frustrated by an injury to centre Anthony Gelling. Wakefield, who were without seven senior players due to injury, gave debuts to Ben Kavanagh, Jordan Crowther, and Ian Kirke, but both Kirke and Danny Washbrook suffered injuries. Wakefield made a good start with a try from Craig Hall, but Wigan took control with tries from Dom Crosby and Matty Smith. Burgess and Dom Manfredi both scored before half-time, but Wakefield fought back with tries from Daniel Smith and Pita Godinet. Burgess scored his second try after the break, but Godinet responded with a try for Chris Riley. Wigan opened up a three-score lead with a try from Lee Mossop and Burgess completed his hat-trick. Wakefield remain rooted to the foot of the table, while Wigan climb above St Helens into second place.

Josh Warrington easily defeated Dennis Tubieron in Leeds to win the vacant WBC International Featherweight Championship. Warrington was never in danger and had the crowd on their feet, but failed to deliver the stoppage that was expected. Warrington was bored by the end of the fight and is looking to gain more experience before chasing a world title shot. Warrington is now unbeaten in 21 contests and has been compared to Ricky Hatton due to his impressive fan base. Tubieron, who had previously been stopped twice, was content to fight on the back foot and was marked up in the second round. He briefly threatened in the third round but Warrington finished the stronger. Tubieron looked exhausted in the later rounds but showed remarkable heart to find a response. Warrington was awarded a landslide victory by the judges. Warrington has been criticized for lacking the power needed at the top level, but Tubieron was still standing at the start of the penultimate round. Warrington failed to deliver the stoppage in the last session before the judges awarded him the victory. Warrington is now looking to gain more experience before chasing a world title shot.

A nine-year-old boy named Tate Ricks went missing after a boating accident in the St Johns River in Florida. The boat was hit by a wake, causing it to capsize and sending both Tate and his grandma's boyfriend into the water. The man was able to make it to shore but Tate was not found. Authorities are searching the river using sonar, thermal imaging, and divers. Tate was believed to not be wearing a life jacket and the search area includes the St Johns River from US-17 to Memorial Bridge to the north, and Pico Road to the south. The Wildlife Conservation Commission is leading the investigation and the sheriff's office is leading the search. The family is staying positive and praying for Tate's safe return. The incident is being investigated as a boating accident and no foul play is suspected.

An Albuquerque man, Sergio Barrientos-Hinojosa, allegedly opened fire at a customer he argued with at a gas station and used his 13-year-old son as a getaway driver. No one was injured in the incident, but Barrientos-Hinojosa was arrested and is facing charges including child abuse. He reportedly fired several gunshots during the incident and was yelling racial slurs at the officers. Police found the gun he threw away nearby. The 13-year-old was reportedly shell-shocked during the incident. Barrientos-Hinojosa is currently without an attorney.

Kevin Carr, a British athlete from Devon, has set a new world record by becoming the fastest man to run around the world. He completed the 16,300-mile journey in 621 days, one day faster than the previous record held by Australian Tom Denniss. Carr ran across five continents, encountered dangerous animals such as bears and wild dogs, and experienced extreme weather conditions. He also had to deal with logistical challenges and traffic. Despite the difficulties, Carr was the first man to complete the voyage unsupported and without a team. He said the highlight of his journey was the Andes mountains and that he had lost three stone during the trip. Carr's journey took him through various countries and cities, including Lithuania, New Zealand, India, the US, and Canada. He encountered bears, wolves, and severe heatstroke, and was hit by cars twice. Despite the challenges, Carr completed the journey and set a new world record.

A Georgia middle school teacher, Nancy Perry, has been removed from the classroom and will retire after she gave students her personal opinion of President Barack Obama, which some parents found offensive. Perry is alleged to have told students that Obama is a Muslim and that any parent who supports him couldn't be Christian. A parent, Jimmie Scott, complained to the school after his 12-year-old son brought the matter to his attention. During a parent-teacher conference, Perry and her husband showed Scott what he described as anti-Obama internet propaganda. Superintendent Chuck Ledbetter apologized for Perry's behavior and announced that school principals are now required to call the superintendent if any board member asks to sit in on parent-teacher meetings. Ledbetter also apologized for the actions of Perry's husband, who shouldn't have attended the parent-teacher conference. Perry is already planning on retiring before the complaint about her behavior. The incident has sparked a debate about the role of teachers in expressing their political and religious beliefs in the classroom.

Sunderland are under pressure to suspend England star Adam Johnson after he was charged with grooming and three counts of sexual activity with a 15-year-old girl. Johnson, 27, has been bailed to appear before Peterlee magistrates on May 20 and faces a lengthy prison term if found guilty. Sunderland chiefs are holding talks to decide Johnson’s future, knowing that if they suspend their top scorer he would miss the club’s remaining six games. Johnson is accused of three offences of sexual activity with a child and one offence of meeting a child following sexual grooming. He has been charged under the Sexual Offences Act 2003 and is due to appear before Peterlee Magistrates on May 20. The complainant in this case is entitled to lifelong anonymity under the law. Sunderland are just a point above the Barclays Premier League drop zone and travel to Stoke tomorrow. Johnson was suspended by the club after his arrest on March 2 but that was lifted when his bail was extended. He returned to training under new boss Dick Advocaat and has featured as a substitute in Sunderland’s last three matches. The suspension could now be reimposed.

James Webster, 35, was spared jail after admitting outraging public decency by using a hidden camera to film up women's skirts in a Lidl store in Maidenhead, Berkshire. He was caught after a fellow shopper noticed him moving his bag closer to a victim. Webster immediately showed remorse and was ordered to complete a sexual offences treatment programme as part of a three year community order. He was also told to pay £85 in costs and a £60 fine. Webster had targeted women as they shopped at Lidl and had been smoking cannabis at the time of the incident. The court noted his early guilty plea and remorse, but also his mature age and intentional actions. Webster had been living in shared accommodation in White Waltham at the time of the incident.

A man from Ashburton, New Zealand, has drastically reduced his income in order to avoid a significant increase in child support payments. Matthew Bird, who previously earned $70,000 a year as an agricultural adviser, quit his job and took a meagre wage of $38,000 a year as a mechanic in order to reduce his child support payment from $1,300 a month to $554 a month. This change was due to Inland Revenue amending their child support formula, which was enforced on April 1. Other parents have also reported financial difficulty due to the increased child support payments. New Zealand MP Jo Goodhew has invited parents to her office to discuss how the new calculations are affecting their wages. Inland Revenue has advised parents to check the information they provided to ensure their payment has been calculated correctly. The Waitaki MP's office has received three inquiries about the changes to child support payments, but none were in relation to the changes that took effect on April 1.

Newcastle United midfielder Moussa Sissoko was sent off for two bookable offenses during the team's 2-0 defeat at Liverpool, with one of the offenses being a reckless lunge on Lucas. Newcastle manager John Carver labeled Sissoko's tackle as "indefensible" and admitted that it could have been a straight red card. Carver was also frustrated that Ayoze Perez did not earn a penalty after being felled by Dejan Lovren. Despite the defeat, Carver saw some positives in the team's performance and felt that they held their own against Liverpool. Sissoko could face disciplinary action for his tackle.

Despite having a four-point lead and a superior goal difference, City's poor form has left them vulnerable to being caught. The team is in need of an overhaul, but there are concerns about the ability of manager Manuel Pellegrini and director of football Txiki Begiristain to identify suitable replacements for players such as Yaya Toure and Samir Nasri. The referee for the upcoming Floyd Mayweather vs. Manny Pacquiao fight in Las Vegas will earn $10,000. Roma ended their four-month winless streak at home with a victory over Napoli in Serie A on Saturday. Miralem Pjanic scored the only goal of the match in the 25th minute and goalkeeper Morgan de Sanctis saved several shots by Napoli in the second half. In the second half, De Sanctis was superb in denying Dries Mertens on several occasions and made a leaping save on a shot from Manolo Gabbiadini in the 64th. The parents of the youngest victim of the Boston Marathon bombings are urging the Justice Department to drop the death penalty for the man convicted in the case. In an opinion piece in The Boston Globe, Bill and Denise Richard wrote about the toll taken on their family after the death of their 8-year-old son, Martin, and the emotional trauma of the trial. Martin Richard and two others were killed and more than 200 people were wounded when a pair of bombs went off at the finish line on April 15, 2013. Tsarnaev was convicted last week, while his brother, Tamerlan, was killed in a shootout with police two years ago. The Richards never mention Tsarnaev by name and stress that they are only speaking for themselves. They hope to turn the page and look toward a better future for their family, Boston, and the country.

A headteacher, David Nicholson, has resigned from his post at The Costello School in Basingstoke, Hampshire, after allegedly using his school email to arrange a threesome with a prostitute. The married father-of-four is under investigation by Ofstead for using his official school email to contact an escort through an adult website and arrange a meeting with her and another woman. The messages between Mr Nicholson and the escort showed her telling him she liked dressing up as a schoolgirl and being spanked, to which he allegedly responded, 'I love this and would be keen.' Mr Nicholson is also training to be an Ofsted inspector and previously worked as a headteacher in Chippenham, Wiltshire. The school's chair of governors, Carol Bode, confirmed that the board has accepted Mr Nicholson's resignation and there are no concerns relating to the safeguarding of pupils at the school. Mr Nicholson is still under investigation by Ofstead.

In this heartwarming story, an 83-year-old grandfather, Thomas Cain, is reunited with a long-lost photograph of his mother, Ora Mae, who died when he was just 12 years old. His granddaughter, Andrea Ferrell, had been searching for photographs of her ancestors and was able to find this one with a distant relative in Florida. When Mr. Cain was presented with the photograph, he was shocked and emotional, and asked where it came from. Ferrell explained that she had found it after appealing for information in her local paper. Mr. Cain was overwhelmed with emotion and thanked his granddaughter for the gift. Ferrell is continuing her search for photographs of other ancestors, including Mr. Cain's father, Henry. The story is a reminder of the importance of family and the power of a long-lost photograph to bring joy and closure.

Honest is a new app that allows users to ask personal questions anonymously and receive feedback from other anonymous users. The app was created by two London advertising executives and harnesses the power of collective intelligence to provide unbiased opinions and advice. Users can ask questions about relationship dilemmas, sexual dysfunction, career changes, and secret crushes, among other topics. The app has received positive feedback from users, who appreciate the ability to ask personal questions without fear of judgment. Honest can be downloaded for free on iOS.

On opening day of the Chicago Cubs game at Wrigley Field, fans were faced with long lines for the bathroom, resulting in some being forced to relieve themselves in plastic cups. The modernization of the stadium caused only two working bathrooms, leading to wait times of over an hour and a potential public health disaster. The Cubs and Wrigley Field claimed the issue began when two bathrooms on the upper deck went down temporarily, but fans were left traumatized and frustrated. The Cubs apologized and plan to add portable units and monitor wait times. Social media was flooded with complaints and pictures of the long lines and plastic cups filled with urine.

A new study by student newspaper The Tab has revealed that students on computer science and dentistry courses at British universities are much less likely to have had sex than those enrolled in Arts subjects like history and English. The survey found that 11 percent of computer scientists and 11,549 students were asked about their bedroom habits. Nine per cent of physicists, five per cent of dentists, and four per cent of law, chemistry, engineering and medicine students were still virgins. In contrast, pupils enrolled in Arts subjects were more likely to have had sex, with just one per cent of Art and sociology pupils claiming they were virgins. The survey also showed that university pupils in Britain have an average of 8.2 sexual partners by the time they reach the middle of their higher education. The survey found that 22 per cent of students didn't lose their virginity until they were 18 years old, with the second most popular age to have sex for the first time being 16. 19 percent of those asked lost their virginity at 17 and 15 percent lost theirs just before the age of consent - at 15. A shocking 1.66 per cent of students revealed they first had sex when they were 13 years of age or younger. The student newspaper also compiled a list of the universities where people lost their virginity earliest, with seven per cent of people who took part in the study following Aston and Ulster with six per cent each. Meanwhile, one in ten students who took part in the survey from Lancaster University said they were still virgins, followed by nine per cent at both Kent and Royal Holloway University. Overall, the study found that students on computer science and dentistry courses were much less likely to have had sex than those enrolled in Arts subjects.

Sam Allardyce is unsure of his future as manager of West Ham, as his contract expires at the end of the season and co-owners David Gold and David Sullivan have yet to decide on his position. Katie, a giraffe at the Dallas Zoo, gave birth to a 6-foot tall baby giraffe in a live stream event captured by 10 cameras and broadcasted by Animal Planet. The labor lasted for an hour and the baby's gender and condition were not immediately known. Katie, who is described as a "diva" among the herd of 12 giraffes at the zoo, held up well under the spotlight. The newborn joins a 4-year-old sister, Jamie. The zoo is proud of the successful birth and the event had watchers both online and in the form of fellow giraffes. Katie's gestation period was 15 months, which is average for a giraffe. The exact number of people who watched the event online is not known. The zoo described Katie as a "toss her head around" giraffe who can stick her long tongue out on cue. Aldi opened a new store in Avlaston, Derbyshire, and gave away prizes to the first 100 customers. More than 200 people queued up overnight to get their hands on deals, including a 21.5inch television. The store will create 29 jobs and has a car park. Aldi donated £250 to the council and children's treats to Alvaston Children's Centre. The store is one of 60 Aldi stores opening across the UK this year. Former Derby County player Craig Ramage cut the ribbon at the event.

A 20-year-old woman named Britney E. Montenegro was arrested in Orlando, Florida after getting involved in a fight involving 'multiple individuals'. The incident occurred at East Pine Street and South Court Avenue around 2.40 am. Montenegro, who is originally from Queens, New York and attends Valencia Community College, was covered in blood but it was not her own. The fight is believed to have started inside a bar and spilled out onto the streets. Montenegro works at Bayhill Eyecare and Eyewear.

Chef Ally Lees of Alfie Bird's restaurant in Birmingham created a giant omelette for Easter, which contains an impressive 12,000 calories and 945g of protein. The omelette, which is three-foot in circumference, is so large that it would take more than five people to finish it. Chef Ally used 150 fresh eggs to make the dish and it took an hour to cook it in a massive paella pan. The omelette is almost five times the daily intake for a grown man and contains a huge amount of protein. Chef Ally recommends a group of no fewer than five people to attempt eating the giant omelette. Despite the challenge, Chef Ally is pleased with the end result and thinks it looks great.

Formula One legend Jackie Stewart has expressed concern over the dwindling number of European races on the F1 calendar and urged the sport's bosses not to abandon tradition for financial gain. The German Grand Prix was removed from the 2015 schedule due to financial difficulties and the Italian Grand Prix is also in doubt. F1 races have been moving away from Europe towards lucrative venues in the Middle East and Asia. Stewart, a three-time world champion, believes that Europe's 'essential' races should remain unchanged and that there should always be a place for them in the sport. F1 supremo Bernie Ecclestone has not been able to guarantee the future of the Italian Grand Prix. The decision to remove the German Grand Prix from the schedule has resulted in a shortened 2015 season with 19 races. Stewart believes that the essential races in Germany, Italy, Britain, France and Monaco should be respected as they helped motorsport become what it is today. He also believes that it's great that new countries are being added to the calendar but that the heritage of the sport should not be forgotten.

A middle school teacher in New York was assaulted by a student's mother and her niece after the mother believed the teacher had put her hands on her daughter. The incident occurred at Alverta B. Gray Schultz Middle School in Hempstead, and the teacher, Catherine Engelhardt, was shoved against the wall, placed in a headlock, and thrown to the floor. Several students were also involved in the attack. Engelhardt was unconscious for several minutes and rushed to the hospital. She has since been released and is recovering at home. The attack was caught on the school's security cameras, and the mother, Annika McKenzie, and her niece were arrested and charged with second-degree assault on school grounds and second-degree strangulation. Engelhardt has previously expressed concerns about safety at the school.

A 24-year-old Syrian national and naturalized US citizen, Mohamad Saeed Kodaimati, was arrested and charged with lying to federal agents about his involvement with Islamic State militants in Syria. Saeed falsely claimed he had not been involved in any fighting, had never fired his weapon at anyone and did not know any Islamic State members. However, evidence gathered during the investigation contradicts these statements, including incriminating Facebook photos and posts indicating his alleged involvement with Syrian militants. Saeed is accused of making false statements during interviews with the FBI and other US authorities at the US Embassy in Ankara, Turkey, in March. He is due back in court next Tuesday for a detention hearing.

Sheffield Wednesday claimed a 1-0 win against Brentford in the Championship, with Kieran Lee scoring the only goal of the game. Both teams played with high defensive lines, resulting in a low-scoring first half. The second half was more lively, with chances for both sides, but neither could find the final pass to create clear-cut scoring opportunities. The breakthrough came in the 75th minute when Lee scored from close range, and Brentford had chances to equalize but failed to do so. The result was a blow to Brentford's promotion hopes.

A man named Carlos Colina, 32, is being held on $1 million bail after pleading not guilty to aggravated assault and battery, improper disposal of a human body, and other charges in connection to the death of his friend, Jonathan Camilien, 26. The remains of Camilien were found in a duffel bag near the Massachusetts Institute of Technology campus and his head was found in Colina's apartment building across the street. Colina had previously been kicked out of the Cambridge Athletic Club after starting a fight over gym equipment and intimidating other gym users. He also has an outstanding assault and battery case pending against him from the fight. Colina is believed to have known his alleged victim and the two were last seen returning to the building together on Friday. No motive has been released and Colina is currently awaiting a pretrial hearing on April 14.

Ferrari team principal Maurizio Arrivabene has urged Kimi Raikkonen to improve his performances if he wants to stay with the team beyond the current Formula One season. Raikkonen's contract expires at the end of the year, but there is an option for 2016 if both parties agree. Raikkonen has stated he is happy working with the team, but his form has not been as strong as team-mate Sebastian Vettel's. Raikkonen has let himself down in qualifying, but has recovered well in the last two races to finish fourth. Arrivabene has told Raikkonen that his results need to improve if he wants to stay with Ferrari. Raikkonen has shown he has the speed and appears keen on staying, but Arrivabene has made it clear that results are the most important factor. Raikkonen will be looking to improve his performance in Sunday's Bahrain Grand Prix.

A New Zealand hunter, Max Verschuuren, is lucky to be alive after his friend mistook him for a deer and shot him in the back with a .270 rifle. Verschuuren was bent over emptying rocks out of his boot on his way to a felled deer in the Te Urewera forest when his friend shot him. He tumbled down the hill in an attempt to escape any further bullets and kept his cool, worried that he would otherwise go into shock. The mate who shot him was mortified and has visited Verschuuren every day in the hospital. Local police are investigating the incident and have issued a warning to hunters to take appropriate safety measures. Verschuuren is expected to be discharged from the hospital later on Monday and has pledged to continue shooting.

A family in Washington was horrified to discover that their baby monitor had been hacked, with a stranger able to control the audio and camera to watch and speak to their three-year-old son. The parents had initially put their son's complaints of someone talking to him at night down to an over-active imagination, but after hearing a man's voice come over the monitor saying 'Wake up little boy, daddy's looking for you', they realized something was wrong. The stranger had also been able to remotely control the camera on the device, and the family reported the incident to Foscam, the company where they had bought the monitor. Technology experts have warned that it is becoming easier for hackers to infiltrate family's baby monitors as many of the newer devices connect to the internet, and advised parents to change the passwords on the devices to make it more difficult for people to guess. Earlier this month, another family from Rochester, Minnesota, discovered their baby monitors and cameras had been infiltrated after they found footage from the nanny cam posted online. The family had first become suspicious after hearing music coming from their baby's room, and when they tracked down the IP address which was streaming the music, they found a web link to a page with thousands of pictures from baby monitors all over the world. The family reported the incident to the police and are now taking steps to secure their home. The family's experience highlights the importance of taking steps to secure baby monitors and other connected devices in the home, and being aware of the potential risks. Parents should change the passwords on the devices to make it more difficult for people to guess, and ensure that the devices are not connected to the internet unless absolutely necessary. They should also be aware of the potential risks of using connected devices in the home, and take steps to secure their home network and devices. By taking these steps, parents can help protect their children and their home from potential threats.

New York Mayor Bill de Blasio is calling for Hillary Clinton to outline her vision for addressing income inequality before he endorses her presidential campaign. De Blasio, who was Clinton's campaign manager in her successful 2000 Senate run, believes that Clinton's progressive history and efforts to listen to everyday people will be key to her success in 2016. He also emphasized the need for progressive taxation, increased wages and benefits, and taxing the wealthy to invest in infrastructure and education. De Blasio believes that Clinton has a tremendous opportunity to present a progressive vision in light of the economic crisis and the struggles of everyday Americans. He encourages Clinton to listen to the stories of the American people to make her a stronger candidate.

A bearded dragon named Liz has gained internet fame for her apparent understanding of the English language. Liz responds to her owner Shannen Hussein when asked if she is hungry, and is rewarded with a superworm treat. Liz is one of many pets on Shannen's hobby farm, which also includes a pet lamb named Winter, two cats, two birds, a snake, and a number of ducklings. Other animals on the farm include turtles, a llama, and what appears to be an emu. Liz is known for her love of superworms and will do anything to get one. The video of Liz's mealtime conversation has gone viral, and she is now an online superstar.

Esteban Cambiasso, a former Argentina international and five-time Serie A champion with Inter Milan, has said that helping Leicester City avoid relegation from the Premier League would be one of the highlights of his career. Cambiasso joined Leicester last summer on a free transfer and signed a one-year deal at the King Power Stadium. Leicester, who were promoted last season, are currently bottom of the table and seven points adrift of safety. Cambiasso believes that the team still has a chance to stay in the Premier League and is determined to help them do so. He has won numerous titles in his career and believes that saving Leicester from relegation is just as important as winning a trophy. Leicester face West Ham United at home on Saturday. Cambiasso has represented Argentina 52 times and scored five goals for his country.

Liverpool manager Brendan Rodgers believes his team's recent defeats are due to their own failings rather than the opposition cracking their system. Despite a 13-match unbeaten run in the Barclays Premier League, Liverpool have lost ground in the race for the Champions League places. Rodgers insists that the drop-off in results is more to do with their own performances than those of their opponents. Liverpool will be looking to bounce back in the FA Cup quarter-final replay against Blackburn, who will be putting all their efforts into reaching a Wembley last-four encounter with Aston Villa. Rodgers is determined to reach a second semi-final in the cup competitions this season. Blackburn showed enough in the first leg to suggest they can trouble Liverpool and will have no fear of their arrival. Liverpool will be focused and determined to win the trophy.

The London Book Fair Author HQ event is a three-day programme offering informative seminars for aspiring authors. Experts from various publishing companies and agents will share their knowledge and provide advice on getting published. Seminars will focus on crime/thrillers and contemporary fiction genres, as well as legal issues and crowdfunding. The London Book and Screen Week is running simultaneously, featuring various literary and film events. The seminars are free with the purchase of a three-day LBF pass.

Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink led Burton Albion to promotion to League One for the first time in their history, but he is not content to stop there. After securing the championship medal, Hasselbaink and his team celebrated with champagne and are now aiming to finish the season as champions. The manager praised his predecessor Gary Rowett for laying the foundation for their success and expressed his desire to stay at the top. Burton Albion players and fans celebrated their victory against Morecambe, which confirmed promotion. The team has two more games left in the season and is preparing to stay at the top. Hasselbaink paid tribute to Rowett for his contribution to the club's success. Overall, Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink and Burton Albion are aiming to finish the season as champions.

Japanese airline All Nippon Airways is set to unveil a new Boeing 787 Dreamliner decorated to look like the Star Wars character R2-D2. The plane will feature blue panels on the cockpit and front half of the white fuselage, as well as the words "Star Wars" in the movie's distinctive font. The trailer for the seventh installment of the Star Wars franchise, "The Force Awakens," was also released, featuring aerial dogfights and appearances by Han Solo and Chewbacca. Fans in the US and UK were treated to a livestream of the Star Wars Celebration, where cast members made surprise appearances. The film is due for release in December.

Josh Warrington will be accompanied into the ring by Vinnie Jones on Saturday as he boxes in front of 10,000 passionate fans in Leeds. Warrington is quickly becoming one of Britain's best-supported fighters and is eyeing a world title in the next 12 months. Celebrities such as Justin Bieber, Lil Wayne, Liam Gallagher, Prince Naseem Hamed, Mickey Rourke, Tom Jones, and Andrew Flintoff have all accompanied boxers into the ring in the past. These celebrities have added some sparkle to ring walks and have helped to create memorable moments in boxing history. Warrington is hoping to create his own memorable moment on Saturday with the help of Vinnie Jones.

PayPal is developing edible passwords that would be powered by stomach acid and include mini computers, aiming to remove the need for traditional passwords and biometric methods such as fingerprint scanning. The company is exploring various possibilities such as edible capsules, silicon chips, and wearable computer tattoos. However, PayPal has no immediate plans to use such devices and the comments from the top developer were meant as blue skies thinking. The company is currently working on fingerprint scanning and one-touch payments to make life easier and payments safer for customers. The latest breakthrough in biometrics is an app that lets you use your face to log in to a website instead of using a password. Security experts have long been concerned about the ease of breaking passwords and the average person having to remember multiple passwords.

Real Madrid forward Gareth Bale suffered a calf strain after just two minutes of their league game against Malaga and is unlikely to recover in time for the second leg of the Champions League against Atletico Madrid on Wednesday. Bale, who was forced off the pitch, has not been injured since October of last year and his absence will be a major blow for Real Madrid manager Carlo Ancelotti. Bale has been a key player for Real Madrid in the past and Ancelotti had praised his performance in the Champions League last season. Real Madrid won the game against Malaga 3-1 in Bale's absence.

Swansea manager Garry Monk is determined to stop his former manager Roberto Martinez from getting a win at his old stomping ground, the Liberty Stadium, on Saturday. Everton has had a tough season and has only avoided relegation by winning their last three matches. Swansea has been in impressive form and Monk wants them to continue with a victory over Everton. Monk believes that Europe has had an impact on Everton's Premier League performances and results. Swansea has never beaten Everton in the league but they claimed a point at Goodison Park in November. Martinez criticized Swansea's tactics that day but Monk put it down to frustration with his own side. Monk holds no ill feeling towards Martinez and wants Swansea to get all three points to surpass their previous best Premier League points total of 47.

A 17-year-old boy named Rahul Kumar was rescued by security after jumping into a lions' enclosure at the Kamla Nehru Zoological Park in Ahmedabad, India. Kumar, who was drunk at the time, had been sitting near the enclosure when he suddenly ran towards the animals, shouting that he would "kill them." Security was able to rescue him before he reached the lions, and he was later handed over to the police for psychiatric evaluation. Kumar later explained that he was drunk and thought he would have a good chance against the predators. This incident is reminiscent of a similar incident that occurred in Delhi last year, where a 20-year-old man was mauled to death by a tiger after climbing into its enclosure at the city zoo. Fortunately, the lions in this incident were asleep and the zoo guards acted quickly enough to prevent a tragedy.

Real Housewives of New Jersey star Joe Giudice has had his driving license suspended for two years and was fined $10,000 by a state judge for having the worst driving record ever seen. Giudice, who is preparing to head to federal prison for bankruptcy fraud, lost his driver's license and pleaded guilty to unlawful use of an ID and impersonation. He was sentenced to 18 months in prison, which will run concurrently with his 41-month federal sentence. The judge called Giudice's disrespect for the law and previous driving infractions and suspensions into question. Giudice's lawyer argued that he is destitute and unable to pay the fine, but the judge refused after Giudice recently got paid $75,000 for prison photos and a tell-all interview. Giudice is an Italian citizen by birth who never became a U.S. citizen and is expected to be deported once his prison term ends.

The greater adjutant stork is a majestic bird that has made its home at the Boragaon landfill in India. The landfill is home to around 100 families who make their living by searching for treasure in the trash. Despite the unsanitary and unsafe conditions, the families are content and have a strong sense of community and spirituality. Photographer Timothy Bouldry has been traveling the world for the past seven years photographing landfills and has become connected with the people of Boragaon. He has found that the people living in the landfill are experts at repurposing and have a strong sense of hope and love. Bouldry lives and works inside the La Chureca landfill in Nicaragua, where he helps the people grow gardens and teaches English and yoga classes. He finds humanitarian photo projects to be the most fulfilling and is inspired by the informal recyclers of the world. Bouldry is a photographer based in New Hampshire and can be followed on Facebook and Twitter.

American rapper Tyga has expressed his support for Arsenal Football Club after being taken on a tour of the Emirates Stadium by Arsenal players Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Kieran Gibbs. Tyga, who is currently touring the UK, was given a No 52 Arsenal shirt with the word 'Kingin' printed on the back as a gift. Tyga, who has been in the headlines for dating Kylie Jenner, appeared to be delighted with the gift and was all smiles as he was snapped alongside Oxlade-Chamberlain. Oxlade-Chamberlain could return to action in time to face Hull on Monday after missing his side's last seven games, while Gibbs will be hoping to start ahead of left back rival Nacho Monreal. Tyga has been in the headlines for dating Kylie Jenner.

The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit has ruled that Asian-American rock band The Slants cannot trademark their name because it is considered disparaging to people of Asian descent. The band, which plays a kind of grunge music called Chinatown Dance Rock, argued that the name was a healthy reappropriation of a term usually considered a slur and that the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office's refusal to grant a trademark violated their free speech rights. However, the court ruled that there was evidence the term is offensive to people of Asian descent and that the refusal to federally register a trademark does not prevent the applicant from still using it. The case has parallels to the Washington Redskins' lawsuit against five Native Americans who successfully convinced the PTO to cancel the NFL team's trademarks because that name disparages Native Americans. The team is appealing the cancellation, saying the disparagement provision violates the First Amendment. The band's lawyer has called the decision 'unnecessarily politicized' and said they will likely seek review of the decision by the full Federal Circuit court. The USPTO declined to comment.

Manchester City will face Crystal Palace's Glenn Murray, who has the best minutes-per-goal ratio in the Premier League this season, on Easter Monday. Murray has scored a goal every 91 minutes, while Harry Kane and Diego Costa are tied for the top spot with 19 goals each. Olivier Giroud and Papiss Cisse have also had strong seasons, but have been plagued by injury and suspension. Chelsea has four players in the top 10, including Andre Schurrle and Loic Remy, who are expected to fill in for Diego Costa's injury. Frank Lampard has a better ratio than Sergio Aguero, but Murray still outperforms them all with a goal every 364 minutes. Murray has scored four goals for Palace this season.

Memories Gourmet Pizza Co., a small business in Wisconsin, found themselves in the middle of a national debate over Indiana's Religious Freedom Restoration Act when people mistakenly identified them as Memories Pizza of Walkerton, Indiana. The owners of Memories Gourmet Pizza were inundated with angry comments and calls, and their Facebook page and phone number were flooded with protests. Despite their attempts to clarify the situation, the owners are worried that the damage to their wholesale pizza business may be irreparable. The two businesses are in different states and almost 300 miles apart.

Exeter, England has been described as "too posh for Monopoly" due to the lack of low-rent areas suitable for the Old Kent Road section of the board game. Despite thousands of suggestions for landmarks to fill the more expensive slots, no one has come forward with ideas for the brown sections of the board, which cost $60 in Monopoly money. Exeter has been noted for its influx of wealthy students and luxury developments, making it difficult to find a suitable location for the lower end of the board. Game-makers are currently seeking recommendations for an Exeter landmark to replace Old Kent Road.

A New York teacher, Madeline Luciano, was fired after an incident in which she allegedly allowed eighth grade students to write insulting words about a classmate on the blackboard. The teacher claims she was trying to teach the students to be kinder to each other and stop the bullying, but the investigation revealed that the girl had been targeted by bullies before and the exercise ended with students shouting insults across the classroom. Ms Luciano is now attempting to get her license back and work in another school, claiming she is the victim of an injustice. The incident took place in June 2022.

A mother who saw crime scene photos of her daughter's body 40 years after she was murdered is seeking revenge. Marcia Ritter, who was raped and choked to death in 1975, was found with her body in a rarely used garage. Her mother, Virginia Trimble Ritter, had been advised against seeing the photos by her then-husband but recently asked to view them. She was horrified by what she saw, describing her daughter's body as having vomit, hair pulled out, and blood on her scalp. Jerome Sydney Barrett, who was convicted of second-degree murder in 2009, was found guilty of Marcia's murder and was sentenced to 44 years in prison. Ritter is now seeking justice for her daughter.

Minister for Communications Malcolm Turnbull is featured on the front cover of GQ Australia in a bold move that has sparked criticism and accusations of fishing for votes. In an eight-page interview, Turnbull confirmed rumors that he had planned to run for Prime Minister if Tony Abbott had been successfully toppled in February's leadership spill. Turnbull has previously appeared in GQ in a sharp suit and opened up about his rise to politics and business moves that made him a millionaire. His appearance in the high-profile magazine has caused controversy, but Turnbull remains confident in his own skin and comfortable with his political stance. In the past, Turnbull had stated that he was resigned to never again lead the Liberal Party, but now he is openly pursuing the top job. The May issue of GQ Australia hits newsstands on Monday 20 April.

A 14-year-old boy from Portland, Oregon, named Jack Cordero, wrote a sincere apology letter and included a Ben & Jerry's gift card to the staff at a Powell's bookstore after he vomited on the floor in March. The manager was forced to clean up the mess, which was described as 'gigantic', but was touched by Jack's apology and the gift card. The letter went viral on Twitter and received hundreds of positive comments. Jack's good manners and apology restored faith in humanity.
base_texts: Indonesian President Joko Widodo has confirmed that the executions of drug convicts Andrew Chan and Myuran Sukumaran are imminent, with all appeals yet to be concluded. The pair, along with eight other death row prisoners, are expected to face the firing squad once their legal processes have been exhausted. While the Indonesian Attorney-General has stated that the executions won't take place until after the Asian African conference in Jakarta, President Widodo has made it clear that it is only a matter of time before the sentences are carried out. Chan and Sukumaran are currently in an isolated cell on Nusakambangan Island, where they have lodged a challenge with the Constitutional Court to overturn their death sentences.

A heartfelt letter written by a passenger named "Bethanie" to an unnamed pilot, thanking him for safely bringing her home after a flight, has gone viral on Twitter. The letter was shared by pilot Jai Dillon, who was shown the note by a colleague. The letter was written in light of the recent Germanwings tragedy, where pilot Andreas Lubitz deliberately crashed the plane, killing all 150 people on board. Bethanie expresses her gratitude to the pilot and the airline for allowing her to live in Spain while splitting her time with family in England. She hopes the letter will spread compassion and understanding among those in the industry. The letter has received an outpouring of emotion on Twitter, with many praising the role of pilots. The letter currently has over 3,700 shares and almost 3,000 favorites. Jai Dillon was unable to reveal the airline or flight number due to security reasons. Investigations are continuing into the Germanwings crash, with evidence suggesting that Lubitz received therapy for suicidal tendencies before getting his pilot's license.

In 2023, Japan's Defense Minister, Gen Nakatani, addressed rumors of alien invasions during a parliament session. He assured MPs that there had been no alien breach of Japanese airspace and no government studies into extra-terrestrials were ongoing. The assurance came after an inquiry from MP Antonio Inoki, who had asked about the dispatch of aircraft to meet extraterrestrial visitors and studies on aliens. Inoki shared his personal experience of seeing a mysterious flying object, but Nakatani reported that the Air Self Defense Force had only encountered birds or other objects in the sky, and no unidentified flying objects believed to have originated from anywhere other than Earth. Previous government statements in 2007 had also denied the existence of unidentified flying objects from outer space, but some high-ranking officials, including Nobutaka Machimura and Shigeru Ishiba, had expressed their personal belief in the existence of UFOs controlled by alien life-forms.

In 2023, a recruitment crisis is affecting secondary schools in the UK, with almost half of headteachers reporting vacancies in English, maths, and science departments. The situation is expected to worsen due to increasing pupil numbers and competition for graduates among employers.
