The survey by the Association of School and College Leaders (ASCL) found that 86% of headteachers had difficulty recruiting teachers for core subjects, while 62% faced similar issues with non-core subjects. London schools are experiencing the most difficulties, followed by the North West and East of England. The non-core subjects facing recruitment difficulties include geography, design and technology, business studies, computer science, religious education, and modern foreign languages. One headteacher in southern England had only one applicant for a head of maths position, while a headteacher in the East of England received two candidates for a head of English position, both with insufficient experience. The ASCL is calling for urgent action from the next government to address the crisis, including expanding school-led teacher training, developing a core curriculum for teaching degrees, and launching a campaign to attract new recruits.

A 41-year-old Indian salesman is facing up to seven years in prison and a fine of up to £186,000 in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) for allegedly cursing Islam and the Prophet Mohammad on Facebook. The man, identified only as S.G., is accused of posting a 'blasphemous' status after watching a news bulletin about the war in Iraq on television last July. He initially claimed he received the offensive image over WhatsApp but later admitted to posting it on Facebook. The UAE has strict cyber-crime laws against blasphemy, and the latest case comes after the country routinely censors newspapers and books containing critical or offensive statements about Islam. The accused failed to attend a hearing at the Dubai Court of First Instance on Monday, and the case was adjourned until April 27. In 2011, a British tourist named Andrew Graham ended up in court in Dubai for calling the Islamic prophet Mohammad a 'terrorist' during an argument in a shopping centre.

In 2023, Marcin Wasniewski, a 34-year-old father from Coventry, survived a car accident in which his car crashed into the back of a lorry on the A444. The crash resulted in twisted metal and scattered debris, and emergency services were shocked that the driver had survived. Paramedics described how the trailer had "literally embedded" itself into the windscreen of the car. Despite suffering serious injuries, including a deep scar on the left side of his face and an injured left arm, Marcin was able to walk away from the scene unaided. He is currently volunteering at a Christian centre while he recovers from his injuries. Paramedics have stated that the outcome would have been fatal if the impact had been just a couple of inches closer to the driver or if there had been a passenger in the car. Marcin believes that his survival was not due to luck but rather the intervention of Jesus Christ.

An European eagle owl, one of the largest species of owls with a maximum wingspan of 75 cm for females, has been terrorizing the Dutch town of Noordeinde for months. The wild bird, which weighs around 6lbs, has been perching on innocent bystanders' heads for about one minute before flying off in search of the next perch. Locals have advised people to carry umbrellas to protect themselves from the bird, which is believed to have escaped from an aviary and has learned to associate humans with food. The unusual behavior has attracted twitchers, or birdwatchers, from around the country, making the village famous. Menno Scheefer, a photographer, traveled 68km to the town to capture images of the owl.

In the year 2023, a 100-year-old man named Michael Juskin from Bergen County, New Jersey, is accused of killing his 88-year-old wife, Rosalia, with an ax while she slept, before taking his own life with a knife. The incident occurred on Sunday night. The couple had a history of domestic issues, but a motive for the murder-suicide has not been determined by authorities. Neighbors, who were visibly upset, claimed that police had been to the Juskins' home a few times in recent years due to domestic disputes. Michael Juskin is reportedly one of the oldest people ever to be accused of homicide. Rosalia was described as a "very sweet lady," while Michael was said to have mental problems and dementia. The couple's daughter had asked her mother to move out due to her husband's instability. A relative discovered the bodies on Monday morning and called the police.

In the year 2023, Sherrell Dillon, a former resident of Benefits Street and a single mother-of-two, has made it to the final of the Top Model of Colour competition. However, her achievement is overshadowed by her current homeless status. Sherrell, who was featured on the hit Channel 4 series alongside White Dee, has been living in temporary accommodation in Handsworth after a mice infestation at her home in Eva Road. She has been striving for a career in modelling for many years and is hopeful that this competition will be her big break. Despite her own struggles, Sherrell wishes nothing but success for her former neighbour White Dee, who has become a break-out star after the controversial documentary series. Sherrell's plight is a far cry from Dee's success, but she remains positive and determined to better herself. The final of Top Model of Colour UK takes place on May 30, and the winner will receive a modelling contract, jewellery, clothes, shoes, and other prizes.

In the article, published in 2023 by CNN, it is reported that a border guard was killed and ten others were injured in a cross-border fire exchange between Saudi border troops and militants in Yemen. This marks the first publicly known military death for Saudi Arabia since they launched airstrikes against rebels in Yemen. The clash occurred in the Asir region of southwestern Saudi Arabia. Houthi rebels seized the presidential palace in the southern Yemeni port city of Aden, and Yemeni special forces loyal to former President Ali Abdullah Saleh arrived in an attempt to secure the city. U.S. Navy warships were patrolling off Yemen in search of suspicious shipping, specifically any weapons shipments from Iran to the Houthi rebels. A Panamanian-registered cargo ship was found to be carrying cement and construction materials and was sent on its way. The article also mentions that hospitals in Aden are struggling and running out of supplies due to the intense fighting and chaos. Additionally, Al Qaeda fighters were reported to have freed 270 prisoners from Yemeni prisons.

The Royal Bank of Scotland (RBS) reported a loss of £446 million for the first quarter of 2023, bringing its total losses since being bailed out by taxpayers to £50 billion. The loss includes provisions for fines, lawsuits, and compensation for mis-sold financial products. RBS was also hit with a £453 million restructuring charge. The losses are a blow to taxpayers, who own 80% of the bank, and come at an awkward time for Chancellor George Osborne, who had hoped to use a return to profit for RBS as a campaign issue before the General Election. The disgraced former RBS CEO, Fred Goodwin, was mentioned in the article as having been knighted for "services to banking" before being stripped of his title in 2012. The losses at RBS suggest that taxpayers are a long way from recouping some of the £46 billion bailout given to the bank during the financial crisis. The article also mentions that Lloyds, another state-backed bank, has returned to profit and is being sold off to the private sector. The losses at RBS have wiped over £700 million off the value of the company and have been criticized by the TaxPayers' Alliance. The article also mentions that the banks were poorly regulated and took risky decisions that left taxpayers with large burdens.

In the upcoming highly anticipated boxing match between Floyd Mayweather and Manny Pacquiao, scheduled for May 2, 2023, Kenny Bayless will serve as the referee. Bayless, who is widely regarded as the best referee in the world, has previously overseen fights involving both Mayweather and Pacquiao. His appointment is welcomed by both camps and has been praised by Pacquiao's promoter, Bob Arum. The Nevada State Athletic Commission, aware of the high-profile nature of the fight, has selected a team of experienced judges, including Bayless, to ensure fair and impartial scoring. Bayless, a veteran referee, will receive $25,000 for his services, while the judges will each receive $20,000. The fight is expected to attract a large audience and generate significant revenue, with Mayweather and Pacquiao each earning a minimum of $180 million and $120 million, respectively.

A hospital in Henan Province, China, named Zheng Gong Hospital, is being moved eight meters a day to avoid demolition for a new road expansion project. The two-story brick outpatient building, which is 1,700 square meters in size, is being moved on over 1,000 large cylinder-shaped metal rollers. The relocation process, which started over a month ago, will take three days to move the building 17.5 meters to its new location. This is not the first time engineers in China have moved a building using rollers; in 2013, a six-story building in Shanghai was moved 38 meters, and in 2004, the Fu gang Building in Guangxi Province was moved 36 meters and took 11 days to complete.

In 2023, 16-year-old Martin Odegaard of Real Madrid was starstruck when he met former Brazil international and Real Madrid legend Ronaldo during the latter's visit to the training complex. Odegaard, a Norwegian international and midfielder, joined Real Madrid in January 2023 after attracting interest from top European clubs. He signed a long-term contract worth £40,000 a week and has been training regularly with the first team. However, he was recently dropped from the Castilla side due to a downturn in results since his arrival. Some team-mates reportedly feel that Odegaard's frequent training with the first team makes him less cohesive in the B team. Real Madrid is desperate for the Castilla side to win promotion to the second tier of Spanish football, and first team coach Zidane must decide whether to keep Odegaard in the B team or allow him to continue training with the first team.

In 2023, an inquest is taking place regarding the death of Margaret Hesketh, a 70-year-old woman who passed away in the Royal Albert Edward Infirmary in Wigan. The family claims that doctors wrongly diagnosed Hesketh with terminal cancer and put her on a Liverpool Care Pathway-style treatment for the dying, which included having her fluid and nutrition drips removed. However, a post-mortem examination found no evidence of cancer, and Hesketh is believed to have died from pneumonia while malnourished. The family is calling for a criminal investigation and alleges that doctors destroyed their faith by leading them to believe their mother had only three months to live. The hospital has confirmed that they phased out the Liverpool Care Pathway in 2014 but cannot provide further details due to patient confidentiality. The inquest is expected to provide a more balanced view of the events.

In the 2023 La Liga match between Barcelona and Celta Vigo, Brazilian players Neymar, Dani Alves, and Adriano helped Barcelona secure a vital win and return to the top of the league. Despite their delight, their denim outfits drew some criticism. Jeremy Mathieu scored the winning goal in a tough game where Barcelona struggled due to the international break. Mathieu praised his defensive partner Gerard Pique for his impressive performance.

Aydian Ethan Dowling, a transgender man from Oregon, is leading the Men's Health Magazine's Ultimate Guy Search with a significant vote advantage. He has around 40,000 votes, which is 30,000 more than his closest competitor. The competition aims to find a man who embodies the qualities of today's well-rounded, active, health-conscious, and thoughtful guy. Aydian, who transitioned in 2009, is a role model for many, with a large following on Facebook. He has launched his own sportswear brand, Point5cc, and is an entrepreneur. Aydian has been taking testosterone medication since 2009 and lives with his wife, Jenilee. He is confident that he will win over the magazine's judging panel, and if he does, he would make history as the first transgender cover star for Men's Health. The magazine has praised Aydian for his active lifestyle, thoughtfulness, and the ability to inspire readers.

In 2023, Manchester Airport temporarily suspended flights due to a reported drone sighting, causing disruption for hundreds of travellers. All flights were halted for about 20 minutes, and some were delayed or diverted to other airports while police searched the area. No evidence of a drone was found, and flights resumed. Drone sightings near airports have become a serious issue due to their increasing popularity and potential danger to commercial aircraft. The Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) has successfully prosecuted two drone operators for safety breaches and has ongoing investigations. Drones cannot be flown beyond the operator's line of sight, must be kept a safe distance from people and structures, and cannot be flown near congested areas or large groups of people.

In 2023, YouTube celebrates the 10-year anniversary of the first video upload on the platform. The file sharing website, which was once known for hosting cats and dogs on skateboards, has evolved into a destination for high-quality content. To improve the quality of its content, YouTube has established "YouTube Spaces" around the world, including one in Tokyo. These studios provide resources and training for independent creators, breaking down barriers for low-budget productions. The Tokyo space has been used for filming "The Crawler in the Dark," a new sci-fi horror movie set in Japan's Meiji era, which will be released directly on YouTube. YouTube is also partnering with Japanese film and TV company Toei to encourage more Japanese samurai dramas, or Jidaigeki, to attract new subscribers in one of YouTube's biggest markets. The financial rewards for successful YouTube creators can be significant, with some earning six-figure incomes through ad revenue and sponsorships.

Sutherland Council in Sydney, Australia, is considering a new approach to deal with the issue of overseas backpackers neglecting popular beaches due to a lack of accommodation. Instead of telling them to leave, the council is exploring the possibility of allowing campervans to park at allocated beachside locations. The beaches under consideration are Cronulla and Wanda, both in southern Sydney. The economic benefits of attracting backpackers, who spend an average of $700 on eating out and shopping during their stay, are seen as outweighing the potential negative impact on local residents. However, some locals have expressed concerns about the potential crowding and the need to rezone open park areas for this purpose due to rising land values. The proposal aims to encourage seasoned travellers, retirees, and campervan users to the areas, while keeping away those who act in an unwelcome manner. The president of the Cronulla Chamber of Commerce has raised questions about where to place the campers and how to do it without offending local people.

Jordan Henderson, a Liverpool midfielder, has signed a new five-year contract worth £100,000-a-week, keeping him at Anfield until 2020. Henderson, who joined Liverpool in 2011 for £16million, was determined to prove himself after a failed attempt to leave for Fulham in 2012. He has expressed his desire to take over the captaincy from Steven Gerrard and is 'over the moon' about the new deal. Henderson's commitment comes as Liverpool hope to retain other key players, including Raheem Sterling, who have also been offered new contracts. Manager Brendan Rodgers is pleased with Henderson's development and sees him as a crucial part of the club's future plans.

In 2023, a 16-year-old boy from Mossley, Greater Manchester, admitted trying to buy the highly toxic substance abrin from the dark web. The dark web is a subsection of the deep web, used for sharing information and trading goods anonymously and encrypted, which has attracted illegal activities such as drug sales, pornography, and hacked information. The teenager was caught after expressing interest in purchasing the toxin online, which is 30 times more deadly than ricin, and showed awareness of its potential harm. He was charged with attempting to buy the toxin under the Criminal Attempts Act 1981 and Section 1 of the Biological Weapons Act 1974. The investigation came after law enforcement officers intercepted his online communications. The dark web has previously been used for illegal activities, such as the sale of drugs and hacked information. In 2022, a graphic designer was the first person to be prosecuted under the Biological Weapons Act after she attempted to purchase a toxin on the dark web to poison her mother.

In 2023, Georgia Governor Nathan Deal signed the Haleigh's Hope Act, allowing the use of low-THC cannabis oil for certain medical conditions, specifically "medication-resistant epilepsies." This bill comes as a relief for families like the Coxes, whose 5-year-old daughter, Haleigh, had been suffering from hundreds of seizures a day and moved to Colorado for access to medical marijuana. The new law will create an infrastructure, registration process, and research program for the drug. Haleigh's story brought attention to the potential benefits of medical marijuana for treating seizure disorders, and the bill is named after her. While Georgia's law is specific to a few conditions, medical marijuana is legal in nearly half the states for various ailments. However, under federal law, marijuana remains illegal, creating a challenge for research and medical use.

Historian David Starkey, in an interview with the Daily Telegraph in 2023, made controversial statements about ethnic minorities, disabled people, women, and the political class. He criticized Doreen Lawrence, the mother of Stephen Lawrence, a race murder victim, for promoting victimhood and violence among black communities. Starkey argued that all forms of liberation require individuals to take control and refuse to be victims. He also expressed his views on intelligence, stating that women tend to be of average intelligence, while men are either very bright or very thick. Starkey, who is born with disabilities, criticized the portrayal of disabled people as victims and claimed that fears of Islamophobia were victimizing Muslims. He expressed his disappointment in the current political class, stating that no politician is equipped to be prime minister and the real talent has left politics.

In the 2023 football season, Barcelona forward Pedro is considering his future at Camp Nou as he is tired of being the fourth man in Barcelona's all-star attack. He could potentially join Liverpool if Raheem Sterling leaves Anfield, as Pedro's wages of £90,000-a-week are less than what Liverpool have offered Sterling and Pedro's transfer fee would be significantly lower than Sterling's rumored £50million price tag. Liverpool manager Brendan Rodgers has shown interest in Pedro and a regular starting place in Liverpool's XI could be appealing to him. Barcelona cannot sign new players until January 2016 but they may sell players such as Alex Song if the price is right. Pedro is also a target for Arsenal, Chelsea, Manchester City, Real Madrid, and Bayern Munich. Barcelona wants to keep Xavi Hernandez and Dani Alves but Xavi is considering a move to Qatar and Alves has offers from several big European clubs.

Newcastle United fans are planning to boycott the club's next home game against Tottenham on April 19, in an attempt to have the lowest crowd in Premier League history and put pressure on owner Mike Ashley. A social media campaign has been launched, and a website called SackAshley.com has been set up to promote the boycott. The campaign has also received support from the Newcastle United Supporters Trust. Fans who don't want to boycott the game are encouraged to participate in demonstrations before and after the match at St James' Park. The boycott comes after Newcastle boss John Carver suffered a fourth successive defeat at Sunderland on Sunday. The campaign aims to unite fans in action against Ashley and increase supporter representation/ownership in the club.

Demi Moore is selling her Manhattan penthouse, which she once shared with ex-husband Bruce Willis, for a record-breaking $75 million. The 14-bedroom apartment, located in the historic San Remo building on the Upper West Side, includes 7,000 square feet of living space and wrap-around terraces with views of Central Park and the Hudson River. Moore and Willis purchased the penthouse and a two-bedroom maisonette in 1990 and decorated it in a Southwestern mission motif. The apartment features new windows, remodeled bathrooms, and state-of-the-art kitchen equipment. The couple, who were married from 1987 until 2000 and share three daughters, no longer spend much time at the residence, and the combined monthly maintenance fees for both residences are over $20,000. The San Remo, designed in 1929 by American architect Emery Roth, is home to several famous neighbors, including Dustin Hoffman, Diane Keaton, Steven Spielberg, and U2 frontman Bono. The penthouse is being listed by Adam D Modlin, president of the Modlin Group, who describes it as the "grandest residence in the south tower" and the "largest intact park-facing residence at the San Remo with private outdoor space."

McDonald's, the world's highest-grossing fast food chain, announced plans to raise wages for its employees working at company-owned restaurants in the US. Starting July 1, 2023, starting wages will be a dollar over the minimum wage. The company aims to have an average wage of more than $10 an hour by the end of the year. McDonald's USA owns about 10% of the restaurants in the country, with the rest being franchises that will not be affected by the pay increase. The move comes as the economy continues to improve and there is public pressure to increase wages. Last year, workers at fast food chains, including McDonald's, staged protests demanding a union and a wage of $15 an hour. McDonald's President Mike Andres stated that the demonstrations did not affect the company's reputation. In addition to wage increases, McDonald's will also offer paid time off for employees who have worked for the company for a year and work an average of 20 hours a week. The company did not immediately provide details on its plans to help workers at franchise-owned restaurants complete high school and college. McDonald's US business has been struggling, with sales and customer counts at established locations falling for two years in a row. The company named Steve Easterbrook as its new CEO in January 2023, and the change took effect last month. Easterbrook stated that the wage increase would benefit employees and improve the McDonald's restaurant experience.

In the year 2023, over 1,700 Chinese students from Yichuan, Shaanxi province, took their high school exams in the playground of their school due to insufficient indoor space. The Grade One students suggested and organized the outdoor exam themselves, turning their desks and chairs to avoid sunshine and potential dizziness. The unusual exam was seen as a way to broaden their horizons, encourage relaxation, and test their organizing skills. The school approved the proposal, and many students believed it could also prevent cheating.

Inter Milan have initiated talks with Manchester City over a potential deal for forward Stevan Jovetic. Inter are proposing an initial loan deal, but City are reluctant to let him go on a temporary basis. Jovetic is expected to leave Manchester City this summer after being excluded from their Champions League squad to make way for Wilfried Bony. Inter's manager Roberto Mancini, a former City boss, is keen on signing Jovetic, who was also a target for Juventus last summer. Manchester City are open to offers for Jovetic if they can recoup a substantial fee, having paid £22million for him in 2013. Inter are unlikely to make Lukas Podolski's loan move from Arsenal permanent, leaving them in need of a wide forward. Mancini is also interested in signing Yaya Toure from Manchester City, who could be one of several players to leave the Premier League champions this summer. Toure, a veteran midfielder, has expressed a desire to play in Italy, and Mancini has expressed interest in bringing him to Inter.

In 2023, Patrick James Fredricksen, a 30-year-old known child sex offender, was arrested for stealing a school bus and attempting to kidnap children. The incident occurred in eastern Utah while Fredricksen was working for a landscaping firm. He had previously left the site with master keys to the complex, and shortly after, a nearby funeral parlor reported a stolen car. Fredricksen is believed to have taken the school bus and used its on-board list of children's names and addresses to attempt to abduct young girls. He was stopped by a sheriff's lieutenant after a report of a suspicious person driving a school bus in the Cleveland area of Emery County. Fredricksen, who has used various aliases, is on Utah's Sex Offender Registry and has previous convictions for unlawful sexual activity with a minor, impersonating a firefighter, and sexual exploitation of a minor. He was dismissed from the Huntington Fire Department in 2003 for stealing clothing and equipment and later impersonated a firefighter to gain access to emergencies and rent an apartment. Fredricksen is currently being held in Emery County Jail for investigation of theft of a vehicle, attempted child kidnapping, and damaging a prison.

Former U.S. Marine Charlie Linville, who lost his right leg and several fingers in an explosion in Afghanistan, is making a second attempt to climb Mount Everest to inspire others with disabilities. He was stopped last year due to an avalanche that killed 16 Sherpa guides. Linville, 29, from Boise, Idaho, is using a specially designed metal foot with a climbing boot and crampons for his quest to conquer the 8,850-meter (29,035-foot) summit next month. He served as an explosives expert in Afghanistan in 2011 and was seriously wounded in an explosion, resulting in the amputation of his right leg two years later. He retired from the service and has been climbing with The Heroes Project, a nonprofit organization that helps wounded veterans, since then. Linville plans to approach Everest from the northern, Tibetan side, along with the Heroes Project's founder Tim Wayne Medvetz and an eight-member team. He believes that his disability is not a barrier to achieving his goals and wants to inspire others to overcome their challenges.

Liana Barrientos, a 39-year-old woman from New York, is facing criminal charges for falsifying marriage license applications during a period when she was married a total of 10 times between 1999 and 2010. Nine of these marriages occurred in Westchester County, Long Island, New Jersey, or the Bronx. Barrientos is currently believed to be married to four men, and at one point, she was married to eight men simultaneously. Prosecutors allege that this was part of an immigration scam, as some of her husbands filed for permanent residence status shortly after the marriages, and any divorces occurred only after these filings were approved. Seven of the men are from "red-flagged" countries, including Egypt, Turkey, Georgia, Pakistan, and Mali. One of her husbands, Rashid Rajput, was deported to Pakistan in 2006 due to an investigation by the Joint Terrorism Task Force. Barrientos pleaded not guilty to two counts of offering a false instrument for filing in the first degree on Friday at the State Supreme Court in the Bronx. She is also facing charges of theft of service and criminal trespass for allegedly sneaking into the subway through an emergency exit. If convicted, she could face up to four years in prison. The case was referred to the Bronx District Attorney's Office by Immigration and Customs Enforcement and the Department of Homeland Security's Investigation Division. It is unclear whether any of the men involved will be prosecuted.

Mauricio Pochettino, the manager of Tottenham Hotspur, has expressed his belief that Harry Kane should win the PFA Player of the Year award over Eden Hazard of Chelsea. Kane has had a standout season for Spurs and could become the first player to score 30 goals in a season for the club since Gary Lineker. Pochettino believes Kane's impact on English football is greater than Hazard's, despite Hazard being the red hot favorite to win the award. The Argentine manager also defended Tottenham's decision to play a one-off pre-season game against the MLS All Stars in Colorado, stating that it's only one game and a good test for the team.

A 66-year-old man from Palm Beach in Brisbane was arrested and charged with a 'breach of the peace' and public nuisance after allegedly burning an Australian flag at the Shrine of Remembrance in Anzac Square on the eve of Anzac Day commemoration services. Tens of thousands of people are expected to gather around the Eternal Flame of Remembrance in Anzac Square on Anzac Day to pay their respects to fallen service men and women. The incident comes just weeks after veterans condemned the burning of the Australian flag at anti-Islamic and anti-racism protests in Melbourne. The man will face Brisbane Magistrate's Court on the morning of Anzac Day. Dawn services will start at 4.28am and big screens will be set up around Anzac Square and other nearby locations to ensure everyone gets a view of the service.

Manchester City manager Manuel Pellegrini is expressing the need for his team to make significant signings in the summer transfer window to keep up with their rivals. City were hampered last summer due to UEFA's Financial Fair Play regulations, resulting in a £49 million net spending cap. Pellegrini has identified the need to bring in a 'crack' player, such as Sergio Aguero, to strengthen the squad. Manchester City is currently fourth in the Premier League, and Pellegrini believes all big clubs need to sign top players every two years. Despite the disappointing performances of last summer's signings, Pellegrini is not explicitly calling for more cash and is focusing on finishing the current season strongly. He is concerned with securing a top-two finish in the league and retaining the Premier League title.

In the current year of 2023, Seattle Seahawks cornerback Richard Sherman experienced a bitter loss in the Super Bowl against the New England Patriots. However, just four days after the defeat, Sherman and his girlfriend Ashley Moss welcomed a son named Rayden into the world. Sherman has since shared photos of his new family on Instagram, expressing that Rayden is the "best part of life." Despite the off-season setbacks, including surgery for a torn ligament in his left elbow, Sherman was named the NFC Defensive Player of the Year by the Kansas City Committee of 101 for his work during the 2014 season. The Seahawks are set to begin their quest for another Super Bowl appearance with a preseason game against the Denver Broncos in August.

A 29-year-old man named Pankaj Saw died after falling three storeys from an apartment balcony in Macquarie Park, Sydney, while on the phone with his new wife in India. The incident occurred on Thursday, March 16, 2023, at around 1am. It is believed that Mr. Saw was leaning on a wooden railing that gave way, causing him to fall to the concrete below. He sustained serious head and internal injuries and died at the scene. Mr. Saw was in Australia on a long-term work visa and had been working in Sydney for some time as a systems support analyst for an IT firm. He had recently returned from India, where he got married.

Howard Ryan, director of Housesafe, inspected pictures of the balcony's bracket and believed that the collapse was an accident waiting to happen due to the railing's installation. The metal bracket appeared to be installed in reverse, causing the horizontal timber railing to rot and the fixings to pull through the timber when pressure was applied.

Grief-stricken friends and colleagues gathered at Mr. Saw's apartment, and his manager, Karen Waller, remembered him as a lively and energetic person who would be missed. Investigators are looking into whether a structural fault contributed to the fatal fall and plan to speak to the person who helped Mr. Saw before paramedics arrived at the scene.

An autopsy report revealed that 17-year-old Justus Howell, who was fatally shot by police in Zion, Illinois, on Saturday, was struck twice in the back. According to a police spokesman, officers responded to an "argument" and chased Justus down the street before opening fire. Witnesses reported hearing an officer admit to shooting the teenager, who had moved to the area from Wisconsin in February and aspired to be a surgeon. The teenager was pronounced dead at the scene, and it is unclear if any officers have been suspended during the investigation. The Zion police chief did not return calls for comment, and toxicology results are pending. Justus' mother, LaToya Howell, told Fox News that her son was not a threat when he was running away from the police. A resident, Bobbie Vaughan, described hearing an officer admit to shooting the teenager and attempting to revive him with CPR.

In 2023, millionaire Robert Durst, an estranged member of the Durst family that operates 1 World Trade Center, pleaded not guilty to a new federal charge of possessing a gun after a felony conviction. Durst is currently in a Louisiana prison, facing a murder charge in California for the December 2000 death of Susan Berman, as well as two state weapons charges. He previously pleaded guilty to federal gun possession charges in Pennsylvania in 2004. However, his lawyers argue that those convictions do not make it illegal for him to carry a gun under Louisiana law. Durst's arrest in New Orleans in March 2023, just before the final episode of HBO's "The Jinx" aired, was timed to coincide with the show. Authorities found a passport, a latex mask, a handgun, and marijuana in his hotel room during the search. Durst's lawyers claim the search was illegal. Durst also faces a contempt of court charge for FBI agents and a state trooper who failed to appear at a hearing in Orleans Parish Criminal District Court last week. The case was moved to federal court on Monday, and Durst's attorneys have not yet responded. Durst is being held without bail due to suicide risk assessments.

In the 2023 Super League match between Wigan and Wakefield, Wigan secured their first away win of the season with a 40-22 victory. Joe Burgess scored a hat-trick for Wigan, who climbed to second place in the table. Wakefield, who are rooted to the bottom, gave debuts to several players but suffered injuries to Ian Kirke and Danny Washbrook. Wigan looked set to dominate with a 24-6 lead at halftime, but Wakefield fought back with tries from Daniel Smith and Pita Godinet. Burgess scored his second try after the break, but Wakefield responded with a try from Chris Riley. Wigan extended their lead with a try from Lee Mossop and Burgess completed his hat-trick. Despite the win, Wigan's coach Shaun Wane was not pleased with his team's performance and was concerned about injuries to Anthony Gelling and Taulima Tautai.

Josh Warrington admitted to feeling bored during his lopsided points victory against Dennis Tubieron in Leeds, England. The 24-year-old featherweight, who has a large fan base and is often compared to Ricky Hatton, easily outclassed the Filipino fighter, who was smaller and had previously fought at bantamweight and lightweight. Warrington made a fast start and picked Tubieron off with punches, but failed to deliver the stoppage that had seemed likely. Tubieron, who had a record of 19 wins from 24 fights, was content to fight on the back foot and was marked up in the second round. He briefly threatened in the third round but Warrington finished the stronger. The fight was interrupted by a beach ball thrown from the crowd and the timekeeper stopped the action almost 60 seconds early. Warrington was awarded a landslide victory by the judges, but some critics have questioned his power and ability to deliver a knockout at the top level. Warrington, who is now unbeaten in 21 contests, picked up the vacant WBC International title and is aiming for a world title shot within the next 12 months.

A nine-year-old boy named Tate Ricks went missing in the St. Johns River in Florida after the boat he was in with his grandmother's boyfriend capsized. The incident occurred when their 14-foot johnboat was hit by a wake from a larger boat around 5:30 pm on Saturday. Tate was not wearing a life jacket and both he and the man went into the water. The man was able to make it to shore but could not locate Tate. Authorities began a rescue operation on Saturday evening and are using sonar, thermal imaging, and divers to search the area from US-17 to Memorial Bridge to the north and Pico Road to the south. The Wildlife Conservation Commission is leading the investigation, and the Putnam County Sheriff's Office is leading the search. The incident is being treated as a boating accident, and no foul play is suspected. Tate is a third-grade student at Kelly Smith Elementary School in Palatka and is described as a fun-loving kid who enjoys hunting, fishing, and NASCAR. His family is staying positive and asking for prayers. The search is ongoing, and crews will continue to look for Tate as long as conditions are safe.

In Albuquerque, New Mexico, a man identified as Sergio Barrientos-Hinojosa argued with a customer at a gas station and opened fire, using his 13-year-old son as a getaway driver. No one was injured during the incident, which occurred late on a Saturday. The father, who was reportedly intoxicated, had his son take him to buy beer at the gas station. An argument ensued, leading Barrientos-Hinojosa to shoot at the other customer. Police, who were holding a DUI checkpoint on the other side of the road, were alerted to the situation and took cover, believing they were under fire. Barrientos-Hinojosa ordered his son to drive away while he continued shooting in the air, discharging approximately seven gunshots. Police pulled over the car near the gas station and found the 13-year-old boy to be "shell-shocked." The father was arrested and charged with child abuse, among other potential offenses. He reportedly yelled racial slurs at the officers and discarded the gun near a house with numerous children present. It is unclear if Barrientos-Hinojosa has obtained legal representation.

Kevin Carr, a 34-year-old athlete from Woolacombe, Devon, has set a new record as the fastest man to run around the world, completing the 16,300-mile journey in 621 days. Carr ran more than a marathon a day every day for almost two years, crossing 26 countries and getting through 16 pairs of shoes. He faced numerous challenges during his journey, including attacks by bears and wild dogs, being run over twice, and extreme weather conditions. Carr was also the first man to complete the run unsupported, pushing all of his equipment in a stroller that weighed twice as much as he does. The route took him through Australia, New Zealand, Europe, India, the US, and Canada. Carr encountered various dangerous animals, including bears, and had to rely on people with short-distance radios to keep a check on him during a stretch full of bears and wolves. He also suffered from severe heatstroke in India and was hit by cars twice. Despite the challenges, Carr said the highlight of his journey was the Andes mountains. He lost three stone during the trip and faced indifference from some people as he pushed his stroller down the road.

A Georgia middle school teacher, Nancy Perry, has been removed from the classroom and will retire after she expressed her critical personal opinions about President Barack Obama to students. Perry is accused of telling students that Obama is a Muslim and that parents who support him couldn't be Christian. A parent, Jimmie Scott, brought the matter to the school's attention after his 12-year-old son told him about Perry's comments. During a parent-teacher conference, Perry and her husband, who sits on the county Board of Education, showed Scott anti-Obama internet propaganda instead of discussing the classroom comments. Superintendent Chuck Ledbetter apologized for Perry's behavior and announced that school principals are now required to call the superintendent if a board member requests to attend a parent-teacher conference. Scott also addressed the community at the school board meeting, expressing concern about the divisive atmosphere and the impact on his family, who have experienced racial slurs. Perry was already planning on retiring before the complaint about her behavior.

Sunderland footballer Adam Johnson, 27, was charged with grooming and three counts of sexual activity with a 15-year-old girl in 2023. He is expected to appear before Peterlee Magistrates Court on May 20, the same day Sunderland play Arsenal. If found guilty, Johnson faces a lengthy prison term. Sunderland's management held talks to decide Johnson's future, as suspending him would mean missing the club's remaining six games and potentially relegation. Johnson was previously suspended after his arrest but was later allowed to train under new boss Dick Advocaat. He has been charged under the Sexual Offences Act 2003 and could now be suspended by the club once again. The Crown Prosecution Service has urged for no reporting or commentary on the case to avoid prejudicing the proceedings.

In 2023, James Webster, 35, was sentenced to a three-year community order and ordered to complete a sexual offences treatment program after admitting to outraging public decency by filming up women's skirts at a Lidl store in Maidenhead, Berkshire. Webster targeted unsuspecting female shoppers as they bent over freezers, using a hidden camera with a lens concealed in a hole he had cut in a bag. He was caught after a fellow shopper noticed his suspicious behavior and alerted security guards. Webster initially denied any wrongdoing but later turned himself in to the police after seeing an appeal for witnesses in a local newspaper. He expressed remorse for his actions and had no recollection of why he committed the crime. The court took into account Webster's early guilty plea and remorse, but also noted his intention and mature age. Webster was also ordered to pay costs and a fine.

In this article, a man named Matthew Bird from New Zealand, who was previously earning a high income as an agricultural adviser, drastically reduced his income by quitting his job and becoming a mechanic to avoid a significant increase in his child support payments. The increase was due to recent amendments in the child support formula, which raised his monthly payment from $1,300 to $1,900. Bird expressed his dissatisfaction with the new figure, calling it "unreasonable" and "illegal," and stated that he was content with the decrease in income if it meant a lower child support payment. Another man, Dean Sorenson, also faced financial difficulties due to an increase in his child support payments by $172 a month. While he considered changing jobs to reduce his payment, he ultimately decided against it, fearing it would negatively impact his family. New Zealand MP Jo Goodhew invited parents struggling with the new formula to discuss how it affected their wages in her office. Inland Revenue advised parents to check the information they provided to ensure their payments were calculated correctly. The article mentions that Bird's office had received three inquiries about the changes to child support payments, but none were related to the recent amendments.

In the article, Newcastle United manager John Carver criticized Moussa Sissoko for his "indefensible" red card-worthy tackle on Liverpool's Lucas during their 2-0 defeat at Anfield. Sissoko was sent off for two yellow cards, but Carver admitted that it could have been a straight red. Carver also expressed frustration over a potential penalty call against Ayoze Perez that was not given. Despite the defeat and Sissoko's sending off, Carver saw some positives in his team's improved performance compared to their derby loss to Sunderland.

In the current 2023 Premier League season, Manchester City is leading with a four-point advantage over Liverpool. However, the article expresses concerns about City's vulnerability in the remaining six matches, as they have been playing poorly and face tough opponents like Aston Villa and Queens Park Rangers. The team is planning a major overhaul in the summer, with high-profile players like Yaya Toure and Samir Nasri set to leave. Manchester City's director of football, Txiki Begiristain, and manager, Manuel Pellegrini, have been criticized for their recent signings, which have failed to live up to expectations. The article questions their ability to identify suitable replacements for key players like Toure and Nasri. The long-term plan is for Pep Guardiola to take over as manager in 2016, but the article raises concerns about City's financial capacity if they fail to qualify for the Champions League. The article also suggests that Guardiola may not be interested in managing City if they are not in the Champions League. The article expresses doubts about Pellegrini's ability to keep the team performing at a high level until Guardiola arrives, and suggests that City's progress could be severely limited if they are unable to compete in the Champions League.

In the lead-up to the highly anticipated May 2, 2023 megafight between Manny Pacquiao and Floyd Mayweather, sales of Pacquiao-related merchandise have skyrocketed in the Philippines. Retailers, both online and in physical stores, are struggling to keep up with the demand for T-shirts, boxing gloves, figurines, caps, and jackets. Fans are buying these items in anticipation of a potential victory by Pacquiao, which could significantly increase the value of the merchandise. Prices for Pacquiao-autographed boxing gloves have already risen by at least 50%, and sales via Ebay have jumped tenfold since the fight was confirmed in February. Even street vendors are making a profit selling lower-priced Pacquiao T-shirts. Pacquiao, who is also an elected congressman, actor, TV game show host, recording artist, and player-coach in local basketball, is widely regarded as a national idol in the Philippines. Thousands of fans are expected to watch free screenings of the fight in covered gymnasiums and public parks throughout Manila. Despite being the underdog in the fight, Pacquiao's followers are confident that he will emerge victorious.

Novak Djokovic, the world's No. 1 tennis player, apologized for losing his temper and scaring a ball boy during the Miami Open final against Andy Murray. Djokovic shouted at his support team after losing the second set and grabbed a towel from the startled ball boy, who was standing between Djokovic and his team during the heated exchange. Umpire Damien Dumusois gave Djokovic a code violation for the outburst. In a video posted on Facebook, Djokovic expressed his regret and apologized to the ball boy and his parents. He acknowledged that as a father, he wouldn't want his son to experience such a situation. Djokovic also reflected on the emotions getting the better of him and the pressure he was feeling after Murray fought back to win the second set. Despite the incident, Djokovic went on to win the third set 6-0 and claim his fifth Miami Open title.

In the upcoming highly-anticipated boxing match between Floyd Mayweather and Manny Pacquiao in Las Vegas on May 2, 2023, the referee is set to earn $10,000. The fight is predicted to generate around $400m in revenue, with both fighters set to receive significant paydays. Kenny Bayless and Tony Weeks are reportedly the frontrunners for the referee position, with Bayless having previously refereed one of Mayweather's fights. Both boxers are in the final stages of their preparations, with Mayweather revealing he is already close to the welterweight limit, and Pacquiao showcasing his skills during a training session in Los Angeles. Pacquiao's trainer Freddie Roach has expressed the importance of a fair referee for the bout, and is confident that whoever is chosen will ensure a fair fight.

In the 2023 Serie A match between Roma and Napoli, Roma ended their four-month winless streak at home with a 1-0 victory. Miralem Pjanic scored the only goal in the 25th minute after a swift counter-attack. Goalkeeper Morgan de Sanctis was exceptional in the second half, saving several shots by Napoli. Roma moved provisionally four points ahead of city rivals Lazio, while Napoli's winless streak was extended to five matches. Security was tight for Napoli's first visit to Roma since a fan of the southern club died following a shooting before last season's Italian Cup final. Roma was without injured captain Francesco Totti and fellow forward Gervinho, but Pjanic made an impact with a free kick and a goal. Napoli may have had a case for a penalty, but there was little protest. In the second half, de Sanctis denied Dries Mertens and Manolo Gabbiadini. Lorenzo Insigne came on late for his first action since tearing his knee in November.

In 2023, the parents of Martin Richard, the youngest victim of the Boston Marathon bombings in 2013, have made an emotional plea to the Justice Department to remove the death penalty from the table for Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, who was convicted of all charges related to the bombings last week. The sentencing phase of the trial is expected to begin after the Boston Marathon this year. In a front-page opinion piece in The Boston Globe, Bill and Denise Richard wrote about the toll the tragedy took on their family, including the death of their 8-year-old son and the severe injuries sustained by their daughter. They expressed their understanding of the heinousness of the crimes committed but urged the Justice Department to bring the case to a close by taking the death penalty off the table and sentencing Tsarnaev to life in prison without the possibility of release or appeal. The Richards believe that continuing the pursuit of the death penalty could result in years of appeals and prolong their reliving of the painful day of the bombings. They hope that their two remaining children will not have to grow up with the lingering reminder of the tragedy. Martin Richard and two others were killed, and over 200 people were wounded when two bombs went off at the finish line on April 15, 2013. Tsarnaev's brother, Tamerlan, was killed in a shootout with police two years ago. The Richards emphasized that they were only speaking for themselves in their argument against the death penalty.

A study by YouGov found that people named Nigel are twice as likely to vote for the UK Independence Party (Ukip) compared to the general population. The research was based on a poll of 46,000 people. The study also identified the names most and least likely to vote for the Conservative Party, Labour, and the Liberal Democrats. The names most likely to vote Conservative were Charlotte, Fiona, and Pauline, while the least likely were Sharon, Samantha, and Clare. For Labour, the most likely names were Michelle, June, and Andy, and the least likely were Nigel, Nick, and Jonathan. The most likely LibDem names were Tim, Kathryn, and Samantha. A Ukip election candidate, Kim Rose, is under investigation by the police for providing sausage rolls at an event, which could be considered a criminal offence known as 'treating' under Electoral Commission rules.

A headteacher, David Nicholson, aged 48, from Wiltshire, has resigned from his position at The Costello School in Basingstoke, Hampshire, after it was revealed that he allegedly used his school email to arrange a threesome with a prostitute while she was dressed as a schoolgirl. The married father-of-four reportedly sent explicit messages to the woman, expressing his desire for her to dress up as a pupil and be spanked. The incident came to light last month, and Mr Nicholson has not returned to the school since. He is currently under investigation by Ofsted for using his official email address to contact the escort through an adult website. The messages between Mr Nicholson and the escort were published in The Sun newspaper, which also reported that he had organized a meeting in a hotel room, which was later cancelled. In a statement, Mr Nicholson expressed his regret and disappointment over the situation and confirmed his resignation. The school's chair of governors, Carol Bode, confirmed the resignation and stated that there are no concerns related to the safeguarding of pupils at the school. She also assured the community that the school is operating as usual and that the focus remains on the students, their learning, and progress. Mr Nicholson had previously worked as a headteacher in Chippenham, Wiltshire, and had joined The Costello School last September. He described himself as a "husband and father" on his Twitter account and was also training to be an Ofsted inspector.

In the year 2023, an 83-year-old man named Thomas Cain was surprised with a long-lost photograph of his mother, Ora Mae, whom he had assumed had no photographic record. The image, dating back to the 1920s, was discovered by his granddaughter, Andrea Ferrell, who had been searching for photographs of her ancestors. The emotional moment was captured on video as Thomas Cain was presented with the photograph, and his reaction was one of shock and tears. The photograph showed Ora Mae as a teenager, and Thomas Cain was overwhelmed with emotion upon realizing that this was his mother. The photograph was acquired by Andrea from a distant relative in Florida after she had appealed for information in her local paper. Thomas Cain's family described him as the greatest, most humble, God-fearing, family-oriented, and loving man in the world. Andrea, who is also hunting down photographs of Thomas Cain's father, Henry, expressed her joy at being able to give her grandfather this happy surprise after two years of searching.

A new app called Honest was launched in 2023, allowing users to post personal questions anonymously and receive feedback from other anonymous users. The app was created by two London advertising executives, Ed and Rob Watts, and aims to provide unbiased opinions and advice from a global society. Users can ask about various topics including relationship issues, sexual dysfunction, career changes, and secret crushes. The app harnesses the power of "collective intelligence" and removes social norms to provide honest and truthful answers. Examples of questions include "My long term girlfriend is bad in bed, shall I tell her?" and "Shall I tell my girlfriend I hired a prostitute?" The app can be downloaded for free on iOS and aims to help and advise users with their personal dilemmas.

In 2023, Chicago Cubs fans at Wrigley Field endured long bathroom lines during opening day, resulting in some fans having to use plastic cups to urinate while waiting. The bathroom debacle caused significant wait times, with some fans missing innings and others reporting that only two working bathrooms were available. The Cubs and Wrigley Field attributed the issue to temporary bathroom malfunctions and high attendance, but fans took to social media to express their frustration and disgust. The modernization of Wrigley Field resulted in potential public health concerns, and the Cubs apologized for the inconvenience and promised to add portable bathrooms to alleviate the issue.

A study conducted by The Tab, a student newspaper, found that students enrolled in computer science and dentistry courses at British universities are less likely to have had sex compared to students in other subjects. Eleven percent of computer science students and nine percent of physicists reported being virgins. In contrast, students in Arts subjects like history and English were more likely to have had sex, with just one percent of students in these subjects reporting that they were virgins. The average number of sexual partners for university students in Britain is 8.2. The survey also revealed that 22 percent of students didn't lose their virginity until they were 18 years old, while 19 percent lost their virginity at 16 and 15 percent lost it at 17. A shocking 1.66 percent of students reported having sex for the first time when they were 13 years old or younger. The universities where students lost their virginity earliest included Aston and Ulster, with seven percent of students in these universities reporting that they lost their virginity before the age of 18. On the other hand, one in ten students from Lancaster University and nine percent from Kent and Royal Holloway University reported that they were still virgins.

Sam Allardyce, the manager of West Ham United, is making preparations for the upcoming 2015-16 season, but his future with the club remains uncertain as his contract expires at the end of the current season. West Ham have already surpassed their points total from last season, but a recent run of poor form has led to speculation about Allardyce's job security. He is scheduled to meet with co-owners David Gold and David Sullivan at the end of May to discuss his position, but in the meantime, he is focusing on planning for next season. West Ham currently sits in 11th place in the Premier League table with 42 points from 31 games, and they will face Stoke City on Saturday.

In 2023, Katie, a giraffe at the Dallas Zoo, gave birth to a new calf in a live event streamed by Animal Planet. The labor lasted for over an hour and was captured by 10 cameras. The gender and condition of the newborn were not immediately known, but signs of life such as moving ears, standing attempts, and nursing were observed. Katie's labor came after a 15-month gestation period and she joined her 4-year-old sister Jamie. The event had a large online audience, with fellow giraffes, including Katie's friend Jade, also watching from an adjacent barn. Katie, known as the "diva" among the herd, held up well during the event, as described by the zoo.

In the article, Aldi, a supermarket chain, opened a new store in Avlaston, Derbyshire, and gave away golden tickets to the first 100 customers. Over 200 people queued outside the store overnight to secure deals and prizes, including a 21.5inch television. The store will create 29 jobs and has a car park. Former Derby County player Craig Ramage cut the ribbon at the opening ceremony. Aldi made a £250 donation to the local council and donated children's treats and baby products to Alvaston Children's Centre. The store is one of 60 Aldi stores opening across the UK this year.

In the early hours of Saturday, a fight involving 'multiple individuals' broke out in downtown Orlando, Florida. The incident started inside a bar and spilled out onto the streets at East Pine Street and South Court Avenue around 2.40 am. A 20-year-old woman named Britney E. Montenegro was arrested and charged with disorderly conduct after she allegedly tried to attack another woman during the fight. Montenegro, who is originally from Queens, New York, and attends Valencia Community College, was covered in blood but it was not her own. An officer used an arm-bar takedown technique to restrain her. Montenegro had a minor injury on her shoulder but couldn't explain how she got it. She also had someone else's blood on her. Montenegro works at Bayhill Eyecare and Eyewear.

In the article, Everton manager Roberto Martinez defended Ross Barkley's decision to take a penalty against Burnley instead of Leighton Baines, despite Baines having a successful record of scoring penalties. Barkley's attempt was saved by Burnley's goalkeeper Tom Heaton, but Everton went on to win 1-0 with a goal from Kevin Mirallas. Martinez argued that Barkley had the right to take the penalty and that he trusts multiple players to take penalties based on how they feel in the moment. Barkley's penalty was well-struck but not put in the corner, and Martinez praised his young player for taking control of the big moment. The incident brought back memories of a previous penalty dispute between Barkley and Baines in a match against West Brom.

In the year 2023, Ally Lees, a chef from Alfie Bird's restaurant in Birmingham, created a giant omelette for Easter promotion. The omelette, which is three-foot in circumference and made using 150 eggs, contains a massive 12,000 calories and 945g of protein, which is 16 times the recommended daily amount for a man. Chef Ally recommends a group of no fewer than five people to attempt eating this colossal dish. He took over an hour to cook the omelette using a massive paella pan and admitted that he couldn't finish it himself due to the excess protein. The omelette weighs in with a colossal calorie count, almost five times the daily intake for a grown man.

In 2023, three-time Formula One world champion Jackie Stewart expressed concern over the decreasing number of European races on the Formula One calendar and the potential loss of tradition for the sake of financial gains. The German Grand Prix was removed from the 2015 schedule due to financial issues, and the Italian Grand Prix was also in doubt due to uncertainty over which circuit would host the race. F1 races have been moving towards lucrative venues in Asia and the Middle East, leading to a shortened 19-race season in 2015. Stewart urged F1 bosses to keep "essential" European races, such as those in Germany, Italy, Britain, France, and Monaco, as they played a significant role in the development of motorsport. Bernie Ecclestone, F1 supremo, was unable to guarantee the future of the Italian Grand Prix.

In 2023, a middle school teacher named Catherine Engelhardt was assaulted by a student's mother, Annika McKenzie, and McKenzie's 14-year-old niece at Alverta B. Gray Schultz Middle School in Hempstead, New York. The incident occurred after McKenzie believed Engelhardt had touched her 12-year-old daughter inappropriately. Engelhardt refused to speak with McKenzie without a security pass and a fight ensued. The teacher was shoved against the wall, placed in a headlock, and thrown to the floor. Several students also became involved in the attack. Engelhardt was unconscious for several minutes and was rushed to the hospital. She has since been released and is recovering at home. McKenzie and her niece were arrested at the scene and charged with second-degree assault on school grounds, a felony, and second-degree strangulation. Engelhardt had previously expressed concerns about her safety at the school and warned administrators about the students' disrespect for adults. The attack was caught on the school's security cameras.

A 24-year-old man named Mohamad Saeed Kodaimati from San Diego was arrested and charged with lying to federal agents about his involvement with Islamic State militants in Syria. Saeed, a Syrian national who became a naturalized American citizen in 2008, is accused of making false statements during interviews with the FBI and other US authorities at the US Embassy in Ankara, Turkey, in March. The Justice Department stated that Saeed falsely claimed he had not been involved in any fighting, had never fired his weapon at anyone, and did not know any Islamic State members. However, evidence gathered during the investigation, including Facebook photos and posts, contradicts these statements. Saeed allegedly bragged about working for a sharia court, openly expressed his support for ISIS, and claimed he had fought in a gun battle that lasted four months. Saeed traveled from San Diego to Istanbul and was in Syria and Turkey until his return to the United States in March. He was arrested in Rancho Bernardo, San Diego, and made his initial court appearance on Thursday, where he was ordered held without bail.

In the 2023 Championship match between Sheffield Wednesday and Brentford, Kieran Lee scored the only goal in a 1-0 win for Sheffield Wednesday. Both teams played with high defensive lines, resulting in numerous long balls but few finding their mark. The first half was uneventful with few chances created. In the second half, Brentford had a decent opportunity through Andre Gray but his shot went wide. The game remained goalless until the 75th minute when Lee scored after a parried ball from David Button fell at his feet. Brentford had chances to equalize, but missed them, including one from Alan Judge who blasted the ball over the goal. Harlee Dean also made a mistake that could have led to a goal for Sheffield Wednesday, but Bus' shot was off target. Overall, it was a defensive battle with few clear-cut chances.

In 2023, Carlos Colina, a 32-year-old man, was arrested and charged with aggravated assault and battery, improper disposal of a human body, and an outstanding assault and battery case following the discovery of human remains and a severed head. The victim, Jonathan Camilien, 26, was last seen with Colina on Friday night, and his remains were found near the Massachusetts Institute of Technology campus on Saturday. Colina had previously been kicked out of the Cambridge Athletic Club after a bloody fight over gym equipment in November 2022. Witnesses reported that Colina had intimidated other gym users and even attacked a smaller man, causing him to suffer bloody cuts and broken ribs. Colina is believed to have known the victim, as they were friends on Facebook and had lived together in Somerville. The Middlesex District Attorney's office is considering additional charges, but no motive has been released. Colina was seen on surveillance video carrying a duffel bag near his apartment building on the morning of the discovery, and police found a saw, rope, and cleaning supplies in his apartment. A pretrial hearing has been scheduled for April 14.

Maurizio Arrivabene, the team principal of Ferrari, has urged Kimi Raikkonen to improve his performances if he wants to continue driving for the Maranello marque beyond the current Formula One season. Raikkonen's contract expires at the end of the year, with an option for 2016 if both parties agree. The Finn has expressed his happiness working with the team, but his form has not been as strong as teammate Sebastian Vettel's. Raikkonen has struggled in qualifying, but has recovered well in the last two races to finish fourth in Malaysia and China. Arrivabene has stated that results need to improve for Raikkonen to remain with Ferrari. Raikkonen has shown his speed and appears keen on staying, but Arrivabene has made it clear that performance is the key factor.

A 21-year-old New Zealand hunter, Max Verschuuren, is fortunate to be alive after being mistaken for a deer and shot in the back by his friend during a hunting trip in the Te Urewera forest on Saturday night. Verschuuren was bent over emptying rocks out of his boot when his friend, who thought he saw the reflection of a deer's eyes in his dim headlight, fired a .270 rifle, leaving him with a gaping, bloody wound on his left shoulder blade. Verschuuren tumbled down the hill and managed to escape further bullets by shouting, "f***en' stop, that's me!" His friend was deeply apologetic and visited him every day in the hospital. The incident is under investigation by local police, who issued a warning to hunters to take appropriate safety measures. Verschuuren, who has received stitches and was expecting to be discharged from the hospital later on Monday, has vowed to continue hunting.

In 2023, a Washington couple's three-year-old son's baby monitor was hacked, and the family overheard a strange man's voice coming through the device, saying "Wake up little boy, daddy's looking for you." The parents believe the hacker had also taken control of the camera on the monitor and had been spying on them. Experts warn that as more baby monitors connect to the internet, it becomes easier for hackers to infiltrate them and listen in or speak to children. Another family from Rochester, Minnesota, had a similar experience earlier in the month, discovering their baby monitors and cameras had been hacked and footage from their nanny cam had been posted online. Both families reported the incidents to the companies that sold them the monitors, but the exact source of the hacking remains unknown. It is recommended that parents change the passwords on their devices to make them more secure.

New York Mayor Bill de Blasio, who served as campaign manager for Hillary Clinton's successful 2000 Senate run, has expressed the need for Clinton to present a clear vision for addressing income inequality before he endorses her presidential campaign. De Blasio emphasized the importance of progressive taxation, increasing wages and benefits, and taxing the wealthy to invest in infrastructure and education. He believes that Clinton's previous efforts to listen to everyday people will be crucial in 2016, given the economic hardships faced by many Americans following the Great Recession.

In the final of the Family Circle Cup 2023, Angelique Kerber came back from behind to defeat Madison Keys 6-2, 4-6, 7-5. Kerber broke Keys' serve five times, including in the final game to secure the victory. Keys, who hadn't lost serve all week, had a strong serve and built a 4-1 lead in the final set. However, Kerber rallied and won 12 of the next 16 games to tie the match. Keys made 57 unforced errors, nearly three times as many as Kerber's 21. The German had earlier defeated her friend and countrywoman Andrea Petkovic in the semifinals. This was Kerber's fourth WTA title and her first since 2013. The match was a pulsating three-setter, with both players showing great determination and consistency on the slow clay surface. Keys had dominated her previous opponents, but Kerber's relentless play and ability to keep the ball in play proved to be the deciding factor.

In 2023, a bearded dragon named Liz, owned by Shannen Hussein, has gained attention for seemingly understanding the English language. In a video taken during mealtime, Liz nods her head in response to Shannen asking if she's hungry. The reptile is rewarded with a superworm treat for her conversational skills. Liz isn't the only pet of Shannen's to gain online fame; her pet lamb Winter is also known for its antics in Vine videos. Shannen's menagerie includes various other animals such as cats, birds, a snake, and ducklings, as well as turtles, a llama, and what appears to be an emu. The bearded dragon looks satisfied after her meal.

Esteban Cambiasso, a midfielder for Leicester City and former Argentina international, has expressed that helping Leicester avoid relegation from the Premier League would be a significant achievement in his career. Cambiasso, who has previously won five Serie A titles and the Champions League with Inter Milan, views saving Leicester as equivalent to winning a trophy. Leicester, who were promoted last season, are currently at the bottom of the table and have not won a league game since January. Cambiasso joined Leicester last summer on a free transfer and signed a one-year deal. He understands the challenge of staying in the Premier League and believes the team has a chance to win matches and avoid relegation. Leicester faces West Ham United at home on Saturday. Cambiasso won five consecutive Serie A titles with Inter Milan between 2005 and 2010 and represented Argentina 52 times, scoring five goals.

Liverpool manager Brendan Rodgers believes his team's recent defeats are due to their own mistakes and not because opponents have figured out their tactics. Despite a 13-match unbeaten run in the Premier League, Liverpool have struggled to create chances in their last four games, leading to losses against Manchester United and Arsenal. Rodgers insists that the team's performances are to blame and that he is focused on finding solutions. The FA Cup now represents Liverpool's best chance to salvage their season, as they face Blackburn in the quarter-final replay on Wednesday. Blackburn, who have already knocked out Swansea and Stoke in the competition, will be a tough opponent for Liverpool, but Rodgers is confident that his team can bounce back from their recent disappointments.

The London Book Fair Author HQ event, in partnership with Kindle Direct Publishing, is a three-day program offering seminars for new authors at the London Book Fair from April 14 to 16, 2023. Experts from publishing houses like Little, Brown, HarperCollins, Headline, Quercus, and agencies such as David Higham Associates, The Agency Group, and A. M. Heath will share insights and advice on publishing. Experienced authors will discuss their career launches, and Kindle Direct Publishing authors will talk about the e-book market. New York Times bestselling author C.J. Lyons and Eurovision Song Contest 2014 winner Conchita Wurst will also speak. The Genre Spotlights will focus on crime/thrillers and contemporary fiction, revealing what publishers and agents look for. A "Know Your Rights" seminar will provide legal advice, and there will be a talk on crowdfunding. The London Book and Screen Week runs simultaneously, featuring hundreds of literary and film events across the city. The fair has moved to Olympia, West London, and Author HQ events are free with a three-day LBF pass, which costs £35 if booked in advance.

In the 2023 football season, Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink led Burton Albion to promotion from League Two to League One, securing their first-ever promotion in the club's history. After their 2-1 win against Morecambe, the team learned that Wycombe drew at Wimbledon, ensuring Burton's championship. Hasselbaink expressed his satisfaction with the promotion but stated his intention to aim for the League One title, stating, "We want to be No. 1." The team will train hard for their remaining two games against Northampton to prepare for the championship challenge. Hasselbaink also acknowledged the contributions of his predecessor, Gary Rowett, in setting the foundation for the team's success.

All Nippon Airways (ANA), a Japanese airline, is set to unveil a new Boeing 787 Dreamliner livery inspired by the Star Wars films and the iconic character R2-D2. The plane's cockpit and front half of the fuselage will be painted with blue panels in the shape of R2-D2's design. The rest of the body will feature the Star Wars logo and ANA's regular blue livery on the tail. The new Star Wars: The Force Awakens teaser trailer was also released, showcasing aerial dogfights, beloved characters like Han Solo and Chewbacca, and the Millennium Falcon. Fans at the Star Wars Celebration event in California and the UK were treated to a first look at the trailer and surprise appearances from cast members. The new ANA R2-D2 livery aircraft is expected to fly an international route in the autumn.

In the upcoming boxing event in Leeds on Saturday, featherweight Josh Warrington will have Vinnie Jones accompanying him to the ring as he boxes in front of 10,000 passionate fans. Warrington is gaining popularity in Britain and aims for a world title within the next year. The article recalls other celebrities who have added excitement to ring walks. In 2013, Justin Bieber and Lil Wayne entered the ring with Floyd Mayweather before his fight against Canelo Alvarez at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas. Former Oasis frontman Liam Gallagher lifted Ricky Hatton's championship belt in November 2008 after his victory over Paulie Malignaggi in Las Vegas. Prince Naseem Hamed was embraced by Puff Daddy after beating Vuyani Bungu in their WBO Featherweight Title contest at Olympia in London in March 2000. Nathan Cleverly celebrated his victory over Shawn Hawk in the WBO Light Heavyweight bout at the Staples Center in Los Angeles alongside actor Mickey Rourke and fellow Welshman and legendary singer Tom Jones. Andrew Flintoff carried the belt during Carl Frampton's IBF Inter-Continental Super Bantam Weight Championship bout against Raul Hirales at Nottingham Capital FM Arena in May 2012.

PayPal's top developer, Jonathan Leblanc, announced in a presentation called "Kill All Passwords" that the company is exploring the development of edible passwords, which would be powered by stomach acid and include mini computers. These edible passwords would eliminate the need for traditional methods of confirming identity such as fingerprint scanning and typing in passwords. Other possibilities for next-generation passwords include ingestible or injectable options, as well as wearable computer tattoos. PayPal is currently conducting hackathons to develop vein recognition technologies and heartbeat recognition bands. However, the company has no immediate plans to implement these technologies. Leblanc stated that passwords as they are now are not effective and that users need to "harden it with something physical behind it." The article also mentions True Key, an app that allows users to log into websites using their face instead of a password. Security experts have expressed concerns about the ease with which passwords can be broken and the average person's difficulty in remembering multiple passwords.

Gareth Bale suffered a calf strain after only two minutes in Real Madrid's league game against Malaga on Saturday, making it unlikely that he will play in the second leg of the Champions League against Atletico Madrid on Wednesday. Bale's injury occurred just over a year after he scored the winning goal in the Copa del Rey final, and he will undergo further tests on the left calf muscle in the next 24 hours. With Bale out, Cristiano Ronaldo and Karim Benzema are expected to lead the attack, as the team won all their games without Bale last season with a four-man midfield. Ancelotti expressed his disappointment over Bale's injury, as he had been a key player for the team last season and had scored goals in the finals.

Swansea manager Garry Monk is determined to prevent his former boss Roberto Martinez from getting a win at the Liberty Stadium when Everton visit on Saturday. Everton's season has been tougher in the second year under Martinez, who led them to Europe last season. Swansea, on the other hand, have been impressive and Monk wants them to continue their form with a victory. Everton have had to balance their domestic commitments with the Europa League campaign, which has had an impact on their Premier League performances. Swansea have never beaten Everton in the league but managed to get a point at Goodison Park in November after Jonjo Shelvey was sent off. Martinez criticized Swansea's tactics that day, but Monk believes it was due to his own frustration with his team not winning. Monk holds no ill feeling towards Martinez and is focused on getting a win for Swansea, which would take them past their previous best Premier League points total of 47.

In 2023, a 17-year-old boy named Rahul Kumar, who was drunk, jumped into the lions' enclosure at the Kamla Nehru Zoological Park in Ahmedabad, India. He shouted that he would "kill them" and surprised the zoo security. Fortunately, Mr. Kumar fell into a moat as he ran towards the lions and was rescued before reaching the animals. He later explained that he was drunk and thought he could handle the predators. The police cautioned him and sent him for psychiatric evaluation. In a similar incident last year, a 20-year-old man was killed by a tiger in Delhi after he climbed into its enclosure at the city zoo.
