Joe Giudice, a star on the Real Housewives of New Jersey, has had his driving license suspended for two years by a state judge due to his "worst ever seen" driving record. Giudice, who is set to begin a federal prison sentence for bankruptcy fraud and failing to file taxes, was also fined $10,000, despite his lawyer arguing that he is unable to pay. The judge's decision came after Giudice pleaded guilty to unlawful use of an ID and impersonation in October, which included an 18-month sentence. His wife, Teresa, is currently serving a 15-month federal sentence on the same charges. The judge expressed concern over Giudice's disregard for the law, citing numerous previous driving infractions and suspensions. Despite this, the judge allowed Giudice to drive home from court but warned him that any further driving would result in immediate jail time. The fine was not reduced despite Giudice's recent financial windfalls from prison photos and a tell-all interview. Giudice, an Italian citizen, is expected to be deported once his prison term ends.

In this article, CNN features the work of photographer Timothy Bouldry and his series of photographs taken at the Boragaon landfill in Guwahati, India. The greater adjutant stork, an endangered bird species, draws Bouldry to the landfill, but he becomes connected with the community of approximately 100 families who live and work there. These residents make a living by searching for valuable materials in the trash and selling them. Despite the challenging conditions, which include no electricity or running water, they are content and expert at repurposing. Bouldry has been photographing landfills around the world for the past seven years, including in Haiti, Venezuela, and Colombia. He finds the humanitarian aspect of these projects to be the most fulfilling and has even moved into the La Chureca landfill in Nicaragua to help the community grow gardens and teach English and yoga classes. Bouldry describes the people living in these landfills as having a strong sense of love, hope, and spirituality.

In the current year 2023, American rapper Tyga visited Arsenal's Emirates Stadium accompanied by Arsenal players Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Kieran Gibbs. Tyga, who is known for his hit song "Rack City," was given a tour of the stadium and posed for pictures with the players. He even dyed his hair red to show his support for Arsenal. As a gesture, Oxlade-Chamberlain and Gibbs presented Tyga with an Arsenal jersey bearing the number 52 and the rapper's usual hashtag "Kingin" on the back. Tyga, who has been making headlines for his relationship with the youngest Kardashian sister, Kylie Jenner, seemed delighted with the gift. Oxlade-Chamberlain, who has been injured, is hoping to return to action in time for Arsenal's game against Hull, while Gibbs is competing for a starting spot with Nacho Monreal at left back.

The US Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit has ruled that Asian-American rock band The Slants cannot trademark their name because it is considered disparaging to Asians. The band, which plays a type of grunge music called Chinatown Dance Rock, applied for trademarks in 2010 and 2011, but were rejected both times due to the disparaging nature of their name. The band's lawyer argued that the name was a healthy reappropriation of a term usually considered a slur, but the court found that there was evidence the term is offensive to people of Asian descent. The court also noted that a refusal to federally register a trademark does not prevent the applicant from using it. The case has parallels to the Washington Redskins' lawsuit against the US Patent and Trademark Office, which cancelled the NFL team's trademarks due to the name disparaging Native Americans. The team is currently appealing the decision. The Slants have expressed their intention to seek review of the decision by the full Federal Circuit court.

Manchester City will face Crystal Palace and their top scorer Glenn Murray in the Premier League on Easter Monday. Murray has scored a goal every 91 minutes this season, making him the deadliest striker statistically in the league. Harry Kane and Diego Costa are currently tied for the league lead with 19 goals each, but Murray ranks ahead of them. Olivier Giroud and Papiss Cisse are also in the top five, but have been injured or suspended for significant portions of the season. Chelsea has four players in the top 10, including Loic Remy and Didier Drogba who can fill in for injured Diego Costa. Frank Lampard of Manchester City has a better minutes-per-goal ratio than Sergio Aguero, but Murray still outperforms them all with his goal-scoring record for Crystal Palace.

In 2021, Mike Premeau and Kathy Danke started Memories Gourmet Pizza Co. in Wisconsin, which gained a loyal customer base and got their frozen pizzas, including breakfast pizzas and gluten-free options, into local stores. However, in 2023, they faced backlash when people mistook them for Memories Pizza of Walkerton, Indiana, which made headlines for refusing to cater a same-sex wedding. Angry comments and calls flooded their Facebook page and phone line, thrusting them into the national debate over Indiana's Religious Freedom Restoration Act. Despite being in different states and over 300 miles apart, the two businesses were confused, leading to a flood of outrage. Premeau and Danke tried to clarify the situation with a Facebook post, but also received messages of support and some sharp-tongued comments from the other Memories Pizza's supporters. Premeau is concerned that the misinformation and defamation of character could harm his wholesale pizza business.

Exeter, a city in Devon, England, has been identified as being too posh for the Old Kent Road section in a planned Monopoly edition due to the lack of suitable low-rent areas. The game makers have received numerous suggestions for high-end locations such as the cathedral, castle, and modern shopping centers, but no proposals for the brown sections of the board, which cost $60 in Monopoly money. Exeter City Council Leader Pete Edwards confirmed that there are no areas in the city that would be suitable for the Old Kent Road spot. The city has seen an influx of wealthy students and luxury developments in recent years, making it difficult to find a location that fits the Old Kent Road description. The Monopoly makers have launched a second appeal for recommendations for any Exeter landmark that can replace Old Kent Road.

A New York teacher, Madeline Luciano, was fired in 2023 after an incident where she allowed eighth-grade students at PS 18 in Manhattan to write insulting words about a classmate on the blackboard. The incident reportedly took place last June, and the girl was targeted with words like "ugly," "annoying," and "phony." The teacher claims she intended to teach the students to be kinder to each other and stop bullying, but things went too far, and the girl started crying. The investigation revealed that the girl had been bullied before, and on this particular day, her bookbag was hidden. The teacher has since launched a court action against the city's education department to get her license back and return to work. Ms. Luciano maintains that she had challenging eighth-grade students and tried various strategies to modify their behavior.

In 2023, Virginia Trimble Ritter, whose daughter Marcia was raped and murdered in 1975, spoke about her decision to finally view crime scene photos of her daughter's body. Marcia's body was found 33 days after she disappeared, and Ritter had been advised against seeing the photos by her then-husband. The mother had declined to see the photos for several decades, even after Jerome Sydney Barrett was convicted of the crime in 2009. But last year, Ritter asked to see the photos and was shown them by Metro police lead investigator Mickey Miller. The photos showed Marcia's body, which had been strangled and sexually assaulted, with her mouth black and her face swollen. Ritter expressed her desire for revenge after seeing the photos. Marcia's body was found near her home in a rarely used garage, with her cookie money missing and cookies scattered around her. The case had been Nashville's most notorious unsolved murder for 33 years before Barrett's arrest in 2006. He had been living in Memphis and was arrested after police matched the DNA on Marcia's clothing to his. Barrett had been in prison on sex charges between 1974 and 2002, except for the year Marcia disappeared. He was found guilty of second-degree murder of Marcia in 2009 and sentenced to 44 years in prison.

In the May issue of GQ Australia, set to be released on April 20, 2023, Minister for Communications Malcolm Turnbull appears on the cover in a bold move that is sure to generate controversy. Dressed in a blue suit, pinstriped shirt, and red tie, Turnbull exudes confidence as the words "Primed Minister" are printed across the page. In an eight-page interview, Turnbull confirms rumors that he had planned to run for Prime Minister if Tony Abbott had been ousted in the February leadership spill. The interview covers Turnbull's childhood and political stance, and his previous appearance in GQ Australia in 2013 is also mentioned. Critics have accused Turnbull of fishing for votes with his high-profile magazine feature, but Turnbull maintains that he is comfortable in his own skin and is not concerned with changing himself to appeal to others. In 2015, Turnbull had dismissed the idea of challenging Abbott's leadership, but in the interview, he expresses no regret about his past plans.

In March 2023, a 14-year-old boy named Jack Cordero from Portland, Oregon, vomited in a Powell's bookstore. The mess was extensive, and the manager and her assistant had to clean it up. Jack, feeling remorseful, sent a handwritten apology letter along with a Ben & Jerry's gift card to the staff. The letter, marked "attention barf cleaners," expressed his sincere apologies and gratitude. The manager was touched by the gesture and shared the letter on Twitter, where it went viral. Many people praised Jack for his good manners and kindness, restoring faith in humanity.
